#3631. 10 Shows Like 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Following the dramatic conclusion of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners way back in 2022, the show has returned for a new season set in the megalopolis of Night City with a standalone story and a new cast of characters (by necessity).

Though the aesthetic and themes of cyberpunk have their roots in American science fiction of the 1970s and '80s, anime and manga of the '90s and beyond embraced the form and took it to entirely new places—so much so that a Japanese/Polish co-production of an adaptation of a video game from a Polish designer has taken its cues from a couple of decades' worth of great anime and cerebral sci-fi. Which is to say, if you're looking for more heady sci-fi series, these 10 are a good place to start.

An iconic, effortlessly cool genre classic, Cowboy Bebop is one of the undisputed GOATs of anime, blending western, noir, and crime genres and setting the resultant mash to a killer soundtrack of old-school jazz (which serves much the same purpose as Cyberpunk's propulsive electronic grooves). The title's "cowboys" are bounty hunters in a near-future in which humans have been forced to colonize the solar system after Earth became uninhabitable. Different settings, but both shows offer up ragtag crews with highly dubious fates. Former hitman Spike Spiegel leads his crew on one nearly disastrous mission after another, their standalone adventures all building to a thoroughly memorable climax. Stream Cowboy Bebop on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

This one's set in 22nd-century Japan, with a slick Blade Runner-esque aesthetic and a setup reminiscent of Minority Report. Here, technology exists to measure intentions, so crimes can be stopped before they’ve occurred, at which point the “criminals” are placed into psychological treatment (à la A Clockwork Orange)—or subject to summary execution because their threat potential is too high. That ability to predict behavior bleeds over into every aspect of life: careers and even relationships are determined in large part by the same systems that sniff out criminal intent. Obviously, this is all perfectly fine, and there’s no potential for abuse or miscalculation whatsoever...though there are a couple of warning signs. The first involves a new Enforcer who becomes a potential murderer himself when he miscalculates the extent of a criminal’s potential to do wrong, and, even more significantly, the existence of a criminal mastermind who is somehow invisible to the tech, even as his criminal actions grow more and more elaborate. Stream Psycho-Pass on Prime Video and Crunchyroll.

Created by Tim Miller and with director David Fincher as an executive producer, this animated anthology series is a grab bag of wildly diverse offerings: Each episode is produced by a different international studio, with the only link between them being one of the three words in the show's title. One episode deals with robotic gladiator fights in dystopian London, another finds us under the threat of sentient yogurt, yet another finds an ambitious cat learning to make use of a family's robot helper. Its format dictates that no two episodes are going to have the same premise, but it shares with Cyberpunk an edgy sensibility and stories set in an apocalyptic future, albeit with a dark sense of humor—its four seasons offer up a mix of tech, sex, violence, and gorgeous animation. Stream Love, Death & Robots on Netflix.

One of several completely standalone spinoffs of the wildly influential 1995 film (itself based on the beloved manga series), Stand Alone Complex requires no prior knowledge. The style is largely the draw, as the series luxuriates in its fictional Nihama City setting, a world unto itself in a future Japan in which cybernetic people hack directly into the internet. Our sympathies are more with the authorities—in this case, Public Security Section 9, a cybercrime and antiterrorism police unit—than the cyber criminals, but the show approaches some of the same themes as Edgerunners with legit punk style. Stream Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex on Tubi and The Criterion Channel.

In this adaptation of the Richard K. Morgan cyberpunk classic of the same name, Joel Kinnaman and Anthony Mackie (yes, both of them) star as Takeshi "Tak" Kovacs. In this future megacity setting, human consciousness can be transferred between bodies. The tech is widely available, but only the wealthy can afford the backups and protections that make it a form of virtual immortality. Kovacs is a former soldier turned mercenary, revived from a backup after 200 years by Laurens Bancroft (James Purefoy), one of the wealthiest men alive. His motives for bringing the man back are shrouded in mystery, but he's giving Tak a chance to solve a very cold case: his own murder. Stream Altered Carbon on Netflix.

Another popular (and Emmy-winning) game adaptation, Arcane is based on League of Legends, a top-down actioner involving online opponents shooting lasers across a map. It doesn't sound like fodder for a show this impressive, but here we are. The League of Legends lore forms the backdrop for the show, but the pull is in the narrative involving two sisters caught up in the growing conflict between a utopian city and its oppressed underclass, without whom it couldn’t exist. The painted animation style is truly something special—not a stylistic match for Cyberpunk, but the two shows both go far above and beyond to create striking visual worlds. Stream Arcane on Netflix.

Vash the Stampede is a hunted outcast with a dark history that slowly comes to light over the course of the series. He’s got a reputation as a human wrecking ball, bringing destruction wherever he goes, and seemingly just for fun—but in reality he’s far more respectful of life than his pursuers. Still, cities evacuate at the mere possibility of his arrival, and a huge bounty sits on his head (no matter that the bounty hunters do far more damage than Vash). He and his friends—actually a couple of insurance agents—find themselves in a series of misadventures on the planet Gunsmoke, building to a final showdown that caps the series with finality. Visually, it’s probably one of the defining ‘90s shōnen-style action series, with elegantly choreographed gunfights that never get old. Tonally similar, Trigun also shares with Cyberpunk 2 the work of legendary composer Tsuneo Imahori, his music being crucial to both shows. Stream Trigun on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

Another from animation studio Trigger, Darling in the Franxx leans heavily into the mecha sub-genre, set in a post-apocalypse where children are bred and indoctrinated into piloting the title's massive Franxx to defend the remnants of humanity. Adults are pretty much immortal, so the kids simply don't have any other utility. Two of these teens begin to develop romantic feelings for each other, potentially complicating their usefulness to society and leading to an explosive, bittersweet finale. Stream Darling in the Franxx on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

What starts out as a relatively straightforward action show about space bounty hunters (the title's “Killjoys”) develops surprising depth over the course of its five seasons. As officially sanctioned Killjoys, the trio at the show’s heart (Hannah John-Kamen, Aaron Ashmore, and Luke Macfarlane) are bound to remain politically neutral at any cost. Initially, that’s a way to get them right into the heat of a fight, but as they develop ties of friendship and family in an exploited community, they come to understand the high cost of unchecked wealth and greed, and the ways in which neutrality always benefits the oppressors. The show’s creators make exceptionally good use of a limited budget and offer up some impressive queer rep along the way, a rarity in pop sci-fi. Stream Killjoys on Tubi or buy it from Prime Video and Apple TV.

Another great cyberpunk metropolis: here it's Kansai, an increasingly lawless city run by elite criminals known as Akudama. An ordinary girl, quite inadvertently, becomes caught up in a major planned heist and is forced to fake credentials as a master swindler in order to stay alive. Like Cyberpunk, the show tackles anti-authoritarian themes among a diverse crew of outsiders. Stream Akudama Drive on Cunrchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

#3630. The Game Awards just confirmed who plays GTA 6's Lucia

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game launches.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East New York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox New Zealand trick for eager players to try.

What is a criminal profile, and how does it affect you in GTA 6?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6's criminal profiles (plural, because Jason and Lucia each have their own criminal profile) tracks how you treat other people in the world, reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. How violent you are, how lethal you are in your encounters, and how you treat people and animals in the world will all affect your rating.

There are five levels for Jason and Lucia's criminal profile, represented by "face with horns" emoji-style icons that are shown on your screen:

Your criminal profile is almost entirely dependent on how often you kill people. Try to incapacitate enemies, or wound them instead of killing them, and don't kill too many police or civilians, and you'll wind up with a Professional or Hardened profile. If you're violent for no reason, kill a lot of cops and civilians, and kill pets or defenseless animals, you'll gain a Violent, Psycho, or Irredeemable profile.

Here are the behaviors that will grant you each of the criminal profiles, and the bonuses that come with them:

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (bullet-time)

Bonus: Non-lethal incapacitations and thoughtful acts to citizens will increase your focus meter (same as Professional)

Bonus: Headshots will increase your focus meter

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Bonus: Headhosts will increase your focus meter, but you will be unable to surrender to cops

If you're a Psycho for too long, you'll gain the Irredeemable profile. While you can move up and down between the other four profiles during the game, once you have an Irredeemable criminal profile, it's permanent.

According to Rockstar, "being irredeemable will have a lasting impact on Jason and Lucia," though we don't yet know what that means. We'll update this guide when we find out.

For my playthrough of the main story, I typically kept both Jason and Lucia in the Professional range, which is the profile I finished the main story with, though I did occasionally drop both of them down to Hardened.

I did this by (mostly) trying to be non-lethal in my encounters, using focus to aim for my enemies' knees and elbows during shootouts. I still killed a whole mess of people in my playthrough.

Here are my endgame stats that achieved me a Professional criminal profile:

*A note on that animal total: I did a little bit of hunting, and I once ran over a cat (by accident!). But most of those animal kills, I suspect, are birds, which have some of the worst AI I've ever seen in a game. They do not get out of the way of cars, trucks, boats, planes, helicopters, ATVs, scooters, and even bicycles. You are going to run over a lot of birds. Sorry.

#3628. Five Smartwatch Heart Rate Zone Hacks Every Runner Should Know

If you've spent any time in or around running culture over the last few years, you've undoubtedly encountered someone preaching the gospel of Zone 2 cardio. Legend has it that easy, conversational effort cardio—also known as cardio that takes your heart rate into "Zone 2"—is the secret to unlocking everything from a bigger aerobic engine to faster race times and even a longer life.

To train by heart rate, you aim to keep your heart rate in the "zone" that gives you the desired workout. The catch is that Zone 2 is easy to get wrong, especially since no one can agree on what it actually means.  Your smartwatch can show you your heart rate, but many recreational runners will still drift into a “gray zone” that's too fast to be truly easy, and too slow to give them a real workout. If you're struggling to hit Zone 2 consistently, there are a few smartwatch hacks that can help.

Pace can be a distraction during easy runs, especially considering all the different variables that affect your effort, like hills, humidity, and general fatigue. A 9:30 mile might be Zone 2 on a flat, cool day and Zone 4 on a hot, hilly one.

Dig into your watch's activity settings (on Garmin, it's Activity > Data Screens; on Apple Watch, the Workout app's metrics layout; on Coros, Polar, and Suunto, similar menus) and put live heart rate zone front and center, ideally as a zone number or colored gauge rather than just a raw bpm figure (though this assumes these zones are accurate—more on that below).

Create an alert when your heart rate goes above or below a target range, delivered as a vibration pattern, a beep, or both. Set the alert for the upper boundary of Zone 2, and you've essentially hired a mini coach who taps you on the wrist whenever you get overzealous. Whenever you hear or feel that buzz, you’ll know you need to ease into a slower jog until your heart rate settles.

Instead of free-running and checking your numbers afterward, build structured workouts that carry the targets for you. In Garmin Connect, TrainingPeaks, Apple's Custom Workout feature, Coros Training Hub, or similar platforms, you can create sessions like "10-minute warm-up in Zone 1, 40 minutes in Zone 2, 5-minute cooldown" and sync them straight to your watch.

During the run, your watch displays the current step, the target range, and whether you're above, below, or in the pocket. Many will automatically advance between intervals and alert you when it's time to shift gears.

Heart rate-based intervals, like 4 x 4 minutes in Zone 4 with Zone 1 recovery, where you don't have to do mental math or check the clock.

Progressive long runs that start in Zone 2 and finish in Zone 3.

Hill repeats, where pace is meaningless but effort matters.

Most watches calculate default zones using a generic formula like 220 minus your age, which can be off by 10 to 20 beats for any given individual. If your zones are wrong, your Zone 2 training isn't Zone 2 training.

Here’s how to fix your watch’s heart rate zones:

Find your true max heart rate. The informal way is to just notice what number you see on your watch when you can no longer speak comfortably; the more formal way is this treadmill test. You can also look through your recent hard efforts, like races, hill repeats, or all-out intervals, and see the highest sustained heart rate you've recorded.

Use lactate threshold heart rate instead. Many watches can estimate this automatically after a few hard efforts, and zones built from threshold tend to be more personalized than ones built from max.

Customize the boundaries. Dive into the heart rate zone settings and input your own numbers. Some runners prefer the "MAF" method (180 minus age, with adjustments) for aerobic base building, and most watches let you set that as a custom range.

Recheck every few months. Fitness changes, and so do your zones.

A screen crowded with cadence, vertical oscillation, ground contact time, running power, and lap pace is a recipe for second-guessing.

Create a dedicated Zone 2 data screen with just two or three fields: current heart rate zone, elapsed time, and maybe distance. Turn off auto-scroll so it doesn't flip to a screen full of numbers you don't need. If your watch supports multiple activity profiles, make a separate "Easy Run" profile with this stripped-down layout and keep a different profile for tempo days and races.

A chest strap (or a forearm or upper-arm optical band) is generally more accurate and responsive than the wrist-based sensor on your watch. For heart rate training, where a few beats can mean the difference between Zone 2 and Zone 3, I recommend buying one. This COOSPO heart rate monitor is one of my favorites, and it's only $31.99.

The bottom line: Your smartwatch can make heart rate training far easier, but only if you set it up to support you rather than overwhelm you.

#3627. Firaxis reportedly cuts a third of its staff as studio head departs and new XCOM struggles

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and said the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age update, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

"The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

Yesterday the internet exploded when it was revealed that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's developing 26th movie in the franchise. Fans had big reactions to this 007 news, and plenty of other figured in Hollywood have also weighed in. I didn't have Brad Pitt sharing his views on my bingo card, but why not?

The James Bond movies make up one of the most popular franchises of all time, and fans have been wondering about who might replace Daniel Craig since No Time to Die's ending ended his run as the character. We finally have our answer, and at the premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth (via Deadline) Pitt weighed in about the casting news. The Oscar-winning actor shared his thoughts with:

I love this idea. I love what he’s been doing. I love his choices, and I think he’s the real deal. That’s great. Good call.

There you have it. Amidst all the discourse about the casting news, the Fight Club actor approves of Pattinson becoming the next 007 after Daniel Craig's Bond films. He's clearly been impressed with the talents for the Twilight actor, who has had a truly busy year thanks to roles in The Drama, The Odyssey, and Dune: Part Three. We'll just have to wait and see what he brings to the table as everyone's favorite MI6 agent.

Now that we have our next James, there are a number of questions about what Denis Villeneuve has up his sleeve for the rest of the cast. Folks are debating who the next Bond Girl will be, but the developing movie will also need a villain. In the same appearance Brad Pitt was asked if he'd be down to play the antagonist in the 26th Bond movie, responding with:

You know, I’d like to do that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It’s tall shoes, but I’d take that on.

Honestly, sign me up. While the response to Pattinson's casting has been mixed, I have to assume that fans of the Bond films would love to see Brad Pitt play a villain in the beloved franchise. This is no confirmation that he's actually being considered for a role, but perhaps these comments will get back to Villeneuve and inspire him to set up a meeting. I'm definitely going to keep my fingers crossed.

The internet is still ablaze from the news of Pattinson's new gig, so the pressure is on for him to deliver whenever Bond 26 actually begins production. The 40 year-old actor is definitely keeping busy, especially as he's currently working on The Batman: Part II.

The Bond movies are streaming now in their entirety with an Amazon Prime subscription. Pattinson and Denis Villeneuve's first collaboration will be on display Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list.

#3625. The Web Is Dead In GTA 6: ‘It Didn’t Feel Necessary For Us’

Grand Theft Auto 5 came out in 2013 when the web was still roaring along. Google search was king. Facebook was a pretty simple website mostly used for wishing people Happy Birthday and snooping on exes rather than a $200 billion ecosystem that mostly serves to create data centers and spread the kind of misinformation that addles your grandparents’ brains. It made sense for the GTA of the era to mock the internet as a series of discrete web pages.Â

GTA 5 featured smartphones, but characters used them to access the open web. A search engine called Eyefind took players to sites like Elitastravel.com and Lennyavery-realty.com. Bleeter.biz was a parody of Twitter. Lifeinvadder.com was a parody of Facebook. Players could visit DockTease to buy boats or Warstock Cache & Carry for guns. Thatâs all gone in GTA 6.

Rockstar Gamesâ head of development Rob Nelson said the team dropped websites for GTA 6 to focus on the smartphone as a gateway to apps and social media rather than the traditional internet.

“It didn’t feel necessary for us,â he told Kotaku in an interview prior to the gameâs launch. âWe definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.â He added that Rockstar might include websites again in future games, but for GTA 6 they didnât serve the narrative in the same way as they did in GTA 5. The development team wanted the focus to be on experiencing the open world and all of the âmeaningful stuffâ players could do there rather than using the internet to buy tons of things online.Â

Itâs also about building a sense of protagonists Jason and Lucia graduating from petty thefts to big heists by forcing players to engage with the economics of the world around them more deeply. The team wanted to create reasons for the characters to be âdoing Grand Theft Auto,â and to create a sense of progression from robbing âlittle shitty liquor stores and pawn shopsâ to bigger crimes.Â

âThey don’t really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically,â Nelson said. âIt was never a top-down, âWe’re not going to have websites.ââ He continued, âI remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, âFor what? What do you need it for?â So, that was it.â

If you’re browsing home security options, Ring has one of the best early Black Friday deals that should be on your radar. Right now, you can add an indoor camera and another one at your front door for less than $65. The Ring Indoor Cam 2K is 58% off at $24.99 (originally $59.99), while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is 60% off at $39.99 (originally $99.99)—both at their lowest-ever price.

Both offer features like 2K video and two-way talk, but the indoor cam is the simpler purchase if you mainly want to check on a pet or kids and see what’s happening near an entrance. It plugs into an outlet, so there’s no battery to recharge, and its low-light color video helps preserve detail when lights are off or dimmed. However, since it’s a fixed-view camera, keep in mind that you’ll need to position it carefully.

The Battery Doorbell is the better pick if alerting you to visitors, deliveries, and potential intruders is your priority. It has a 140-degree horizontal and vertical field of view that provides head-to-toe framing, plus up to 6x zoom for better detail. You can install it without wiring, though you’ll need to recharge its built-in battery. It also requires a 2.4GHz wifi network.

The main catch with both devices is the ongoing subscription cost: Live viewing, two-way talk, and basic real-time notifications all work without a subscription, but reviewing saved footage requires a paid plan, starting at $4.99 per month or $49.99 annually for one device; coverage for multiple devices at one location starts at $9.99 monthly or $99.99 annually.

At these prices, the Ring Indoor Cam 2K is perfect for occasional live check-ins, while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is better suited to monitoring your front entrance. Buying both makes sense if you already have a Ring plan that covers extra devices.

#3621. GTA 6′s Map Contains Areas That Could Be Used In The ‘Future,’ Says Rockstar

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the largest open world Rockstar has ever created. It’s a map filled with locations to explore. However, after playing over 130 hours of GTA 6, there were still plenty of locations, including a zoo and a small northern town, that I never visited once during the story. And according to Rockstar, that’s because the map in GTA 6 was built for the “future.”

Ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6‘s launch, I asked Rockstar about the inclusion of at least two large casinos on the map. These locations can’t be entered and are never referenced or visited in the story or in any of the side missions I played. So I asked why Rockstar didn’t let Jason and Lucia bet it all on red.

âJason and Luciaâs story didnât feel like the right place for us to introduce gambling,” explained Rockstar VP of design Stephen Donkin. “Especially with the fine balance we sought throughout the economy.”

That’s fair. GTA 6 is the first Grand Theft Auto game to really make money feel important, and at times it can be hard to scrounge together enough cash to buy a new gun or fix up your car. So letting players save-scum their way to victory at the casino and have the characters come away with tens of thousands of dollars or more could have derailed the story Rockstar was trying to tell. But those casinos and other unused locations, like an extremely detailed zoo and a large graveyard, could end up being used for…something in the future.

“The map has been built for the long term and with many factors in mind,” said Donkin. “So there are a few areas on the map that give us options in the future should we have a gameplay or narrative need for them.â

Rockstar didn’t share any more details with me about what those “needs” could be, but it does seem that the company has built GTA 6 as something it can expand upon over time, possibly with expansions, updates, and/or some kind of online mode. For now, there’s plenty of GTA 6 for players to get lost in, and even those out-of-the-way locations are fun to explore.

#3620. Former GTA 4 and Red Dead boss thinks "we are one Toy Story moment away" from people accepting gen-AI in game development in the West

"In the East, they've already accepted it."

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

"When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it."

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it."

Feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay."

Feder views gen-AI simply as new technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder said of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected."

There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

It’s been very clear from the opening (express pass-oriented) episode of The Amazing Race 39 that producers were hoping for an all-women team to win. The season started out with five all-women teams, and subsequent episodes have noted various milestones the ladies have hit and more. On one level, it’s been nice to see so many ladies in the mix. Yet, because of the way gameplay has been set up, the same mixed gender teams were targeted myriad times, and that has meant two INCREDIBLE teams have not really being treated as threats.

I'm about to get into spoiler's for last week's "Million Dollar Moves" episode on the 2026 TV schedule, including who was eliminated, so heads up! Still with me? Great.

Hear me out, because I’m about to semi-talk some smack about the games Ali & Joanna and Anne-Marie & Riley have played, and I want to make it clear I like both teams. They’re good TV. They’re strong competitors. I especially appreciate the likable personalities both teams have exhibited. The soccer pals and mother-daughter duo have great respect for their partners, but because of the way the new season was put together and edited they have just skated by.

Because Ali & Joanna aligned with Ann-Marie & Riley early on, they’ve had a big advantage compared to a lot of other teams. I don’t think anyone is really on the look out for them, either, despite the fact both teams have earned a first place finish twice. They are threats, but because the mixed gender team of Michelle & Matt was highlighted as “the big threat” and went on a midseason three-episode winning tear, these other two teams have stayed under the radar.

Listen, I feel like The Amazing Race producers knew Matt & Michelle would be targeted in the double U-Turn, but they and Daisha and Dalton prevailed anyway during that first live round. Then, the next week they set up a second double U-Turn, and of course Matt & Michelle were targeted again. Phil called the couple “dynamic” in this BTS Race video, and given how fun they were to watch, I wish things would have shaken out a bit differently so another (or other) teams were targeted that second episode, but that is what it is.

The bigger problem, however? The way the challenge was set up led to all of the other teams working together. Everyone huddled together and gave each other answers like they were cheating on a pop quiz, and then Matt & Michelle had to go it alone. They also had to do both sides of the challenge with no help. Yes, struggling with directions didn’t help, but they were at a heavy disadvantage due to being targeted. The other teams weren’t.

I’m sure TAR would call it fair gameplay. I call it boring TV.

The thing is, as a former soccer player myself, I get the competitive attitude, and I’d love to see Ali & Joanna win. I’ve actually felt that way even before Michelle & Matt started dominating. I think it’s probably a strength for the two leading lady teams they’re both just skating by under-the-radar this season. If I were them, I’d be extremely happy about this outcome and the way the show has ultimately set them up for success.

I honestly more blame the set up of the race this season for creating a non-compelling narrative. Allowing teams to “work together” has been a point of contention on The Amazing Race for a long time. (Like I can remember a major incident back in Season 32, so years, and producers have even discussed making changes before.)

There’s always a question of “where is the line,” right? Is it OK to give another team directions or point them in the right direction with a clue? I’d argue yes. Is it OK to work together on a detail-oriented counting challenge 100% so that the colluding teams all finish together? Even if the Race says that’s fine, I’d argue those episodes make the show go from a 9/10 to a 2/10 for those who are watching.

Just something to consider, Race producers.

Anyway, this “working together” philosophy has certainly helped Ali & Joanna and Ann-Marie & Riley get through a lot of challenges this season, and they’ve managed to do it with most of the other teams being none the wiser, or at least not seeing them as real threats to win. There's a lot of money at stake, and per TAR’s rules, they aren’t doing anything wrong. Still, if an all-women team wins this season, I would have liked it way better if they’d done it on their own merit, and not because of some Amazing Race challenge loopholes.

#3618. Blizzard suspends World of Warcraft: Forever gold exploit abusers, puts trading blocks on their accounts and removes ill-gotten funds for good measure

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

"As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest."

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

"Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers."

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse."

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

#3617. Apple Won't Make a Small Phone so This Company Is Stepping In

Big smartphones have long been the norm. It seems many, if not most, of us prefer our smartphones to be akin to tiny tablets. Even Apple's smallest iPhone isn't that small, with a 6.1-inch display. (Compare that to the 5.4-inch iPhone mini it used to sell.) But just because a lot of us like it that way doesn't mean all of us do.

Despite what companies like Apple would lead you to believe, there are plenty of people out there who want their smartphones to be smaller. For some, the iPhone mini was perfect, featuring a design that most could use comfortably with one hand. While the sales might not have been steady enough for Apple to continue producing the mini line, anecdotally, I know quite a few people who would happily keep using iPhones this small, if only Apple would make more of them. Perhaps you know people like this too; maybe you're one of them.

While the rumor mill does not suggest that Apple plans to make a new iPhone mini, that doesn't mean the dream of the tiny smartphone is dead. Enter "Enough Phone," a new device with a humble goal: to create a "small, modern smartphone that's enough."

Enough Phone really does seem small. The company says its upcoming device is 133mm by 64mm, and less than 12mm thick. That's the equivalent of 5.24 inches by 2.52 inches, and less than 0.47 inches thick. It's remarkably similar to the iPhone 13 mini, at 5.18 by 2.53 inches, and 0.3 inches thick. While the Enough Phone might be a tad larger overall, and perhaps noticeably thicker, it's still reminiscent of that "mini" footprint.

The Enough Phone's 5.3-inch display isn't particularly modern, however. While we don't know the display type, we do know that it has a resolution of 1520 x 720, which may look less sharp to anyone coming from the 2340 x 1080 resolution of the iPhone 13 mini. I'd wager that most people interested in a device like this aren't looking for an ultra-sharp OLED display anyway, but it's worth noting here.

As for the Enough Phone's other specs, the company says it plans to pack in a 2.4GHz MediaTek Dimensity 7500 chip with 8GB of RAM, 128GB of built-in storage, though you can expand that with a microSD card (something you don't see on many smartphones these days). The current plan is to ship with a single 50MP Sony IMX766 rear camera, and a 32MP selfie cam, which would be amongst the highest-resolution front-facing cameras on any smartphone. It supports 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and eSIM, with the option to use a physical SIM as well.

Enough is also aiming to make its smartphone more repairable than the competition. While smartphone OEMs have made slight improvements to repairability in recent years, few phones are made to be opened up by the user, and their components replaced. While Enough Phone isn't fully modular, it is designed with easy-to-open screws, and comes with a fully replaceable 3,500 mAh battery. Combined with promised software support through 2032, Enough says this device "should last you into the next decade."

Now, all of these specs are targets, as the phone is currently in the prototype stage. Enough says that final details may change "slightly" during testing. I would at least hope that the dimensions, particularly the screen size, remain the same by launch. What will likely stay the same, however, are the ringtones: Enough says they hired composer Brian Squillance of LAANDS to produce the jingles for its phone, which is a neat touch.

Unfortunately for Apple fans, however, Enough Phone isn't an iPhone. That said, it doesn't have to be an Android phone, either. While you can buy the phone with Android 17 installed, you can also choose to run OdysseyOS, a minimalist "de-Googled" operating system made by SLEKE. Enough says OdysseyOS is meant for "intentional phone use," which might appeal to anyone looking for a phone that's "dumb" as well as small.

Of course, neither operating system is iOS. Unfortunately for Apple users, the only true iPhone options here are to continue using an old iPhone mini, which Apple does still support, or to opt for an iPhone 17e, the smallest iPhone the company currently makes. It's pretty easy to find a used and refurbished iPhone 13 mini for reasonable price; but while they can still run the latest version of iOS, you won't be able to take advantage of all of Apple's newest features. Plus, while there's no telling how long Apple plans to support the 13 line for, it won't support it forever—by iOS 28 or iOS 29, your phone might lose support entirely.

If the promise of a modern mini smartphone entices you, you can back the Enough Phone on Kickstarter today. While the company's $399 "Super Early Bird" reward is already sold out, as of this article, the "Early Bird" reward is still up. That reward costs $449, and includes a glass screen protector pre-installed, a protective case, a USB-C cable, a USB-C to 3.5mm headphone adapter, a hex screwdriver, and green "Founders' Edition" backplate screws. Enough says that the retail price for its phone will be $599 after the campaign, so you can save $150 by backing the phone today—if you're serious about small phones. The Enough Phone is slated for a May 2027 launch.

After Jensen Huang's departure from the company last week, Nvidia is now on the hunt for its next permanent CEO. Speaking in the Q&A section of Nvidia's Q3 2027 earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones says the directors are taking the search "very seriously."

"We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates" says Jones. "The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully."

Jones also says the company "won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person," but Amazon boss Jeff Bezos seems to think that hiring outside of Nvidia would be a mistake.

"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," says Bezos, speaking at the Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday (via Yahoo Finance). "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding, and so I would always think that's a last resort."

Nvidia is currently being helmed by CFO Collette Kress as an interim chief, while recent reports have suggested that Huang may make a potential return to the company.

The ex-Nvidia chief said that he would come back "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America" after a petition calling for his reinstatement, but Nvidia's board has poured cold water on this idea already.

"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," says Jones during the earnings call opening statements.

#3615. Here’s What Gets Added To A GTA Game Right Before Launch

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rob NelsonRockstar Games

Some big games go gold months before release, meaning theyâre feature-complete and certified to be printed on discs or cartridges for the relevant consoles theyâre coming out on. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick waited until a week before Grand Theft Auto 6âs launch to confirm with 100 percent certainty that it wouldnât get another delay. So what sorts of stuff does Rockstar Games tinker with in the final stretch of a years-long development process?

According to head of production Rob Nelson, it can be adding a last-minute piece of music or tinkering with the open-world polish. In a recent interview with Kotaku, he explained that the team begins to âcircle the wagonsâ two to three months out from launch to see what final fixes, improvements, and additions are achievable before the gameâs initial release.Â

The changes need to get progressively smaller, or they risk creating other problems that can cause last-minute trouble. âWhen you go and you’re messing around with systemic stuff, it’s quite scary,â he said. âWhereas if you’re fixing a piece of scripted content on a mission, less scary, because as long as you fix it there, it’s fine.â

Nelson mentioned that the partner mechanics between protagonists Jason and Lucia were something the team did several final passes on to get just right. He said the free-roam mechanic with the two of them together was particularly challenging to finesse.Â

âIt’s like if you’re going around as them together, it has to hold up if you go into a shop together and buy something, you buy something for the partner, or you go into a club and you can dance together or you go in and you pull a gun on somebody, you jack a carâlike, it has to work,â he told Kotaku. âYou have to basically be able to play Grand Theft Auto with a partner, an AI partner.â

This could include small stuff like suddenly exiting a store or hopping out of a car. Whichever character the player isnât controlling in that moment has to respond immediately and in a way that feels natural. Spontaneity can feel liberating, but it can also lead to jank, and Rockstar wanted to avoid the potential messiness that can come from too much unpredictability.Â

Nelson gave an example of when players go into gang compounds. If Jason or Lucia go to choke someone during stealth, the other will try to follow suit. The same goes for pulling out guns and shooting. This complexity can lead the characters to make mistakes in real time, which is supposed to flow into the larger narrative.Â

âIn that moment you have to make a choice, not as a player but as a partner: Am I going to leave them?â Nelson said. âOr I’m going to start shooting this cop, is that going to then fuck with my criminal profiles? And you have all of this stuff that you’re juggling.â He believes even the messiness of a pathing error can be additive to that sort of experience.Â

Aside from polishing free-roam interactions and scripted sequences, the team spent the final months tinkering with GTA 6âs economy, relationship metrics, and criminal profiles, the reputations that drive how the world reacts to Jason and Lucia. No doubt some or all of that will continue to get tweaked in a parade of post-launch patches during the gameâs first year and beyond.Â

#3614. "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early

New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first."

For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

We’ve known for a while that Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson would be returning for a small gig in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. But knowing something will happen and seeing it on the carpet are two separate things. Of course, all eyes were on the two original stars (and Elizabeth Banks and Woody Harrelson) during last night’s New York premiere. To the point I almost missed the coolest floating shoulder dress.

Note I said shoulder and not shoulders. We’ve seen Florence Pugh and Emily Blunt rock the plural version before, but Sunrise on the Reaping’s Whitney Peak took the look to a new level and used the fashion trend as a perch for a white bird on the movie's (fittingly) purple carpet. Take a look.

The perched bird really fits into the vibe the ladies of Panem have created in recent weeks. Mckenna Grace has dropped all the Hunger Games looks, and paid homage to Jennifer Lawrence many times. Elle Fanning has gotten into the Capitol-themed dressing in recent weeks. The whole thing has been really fun to watch play out. Now, Whitney Peak, who plays Haymitch’s “love” Lenore Dove – herself a mirror to Lucy Gray – has her own viral look.

Of course, even when you are wearing a gorgeous deep blue gown with perfect theming and an intricate shoulder, it’s hard to compete with the fan service of seeing the OGs on a Hunger Games carpet again. It’s difficult to believe it’s been 11 years since the last Katniss Everdeen story graced the big screen, but time has passed. The cast still looks great, though.

Suzanne Collins’ return to Panem with Sunrise on the Reaping was an exceptionally well-reviewed (if a bit bleak) book. The trailer for Reaping has looked astounding and first reactions are coming in. The movie officially hits the 2026 release schedule on November 20th, and while this was the big premiere, I hope that means we have a couple more days of fun celebrity fashion to go.

#3612. I’m a Deals Writer, and These Are My Top 10 Tech Deals This Week

As Lifehacker's deals writer, I'm always looking for the best bargains on TVs, speakers, laptops, and other tech. Now that it's Friday, I've gathered together this week's sales highlights, all of which I've vetted using my favorite price-tracking tools to make sure they are actually good deals.

This week, you can already feel the early Black Friday deals heating up with price cuts on the M5 MacBook Air, Bose speakers and headphones, a Samsung OLED TV, and more.

The MacBook Air with the M5 chip comes in both 13-inch and 15-inch sizes, and if you're interested in either, it's a good time to buy: Amazon is selling both right now at a $200 discount. That brings the 13-inch MacBook Air to $1,099.99 (down from $1,299) and the 15-inch MacBook Air to $1,299 (originally $1,499), reaching their lowest prices since the June price hikes.

The WH-1000XM5 headphones were at the top of their class until they were supplanted by the XM6s. On the plus side, by virtue of being older, they're currently discounted to $198 (originally $399.99). These are still incredible headphones in 2026, and with a $200 discount, they are a steal.

Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Headphones are down to $199 from $359, saving you $160 and bringing them to their lowest price yet. Weighing around 8.1 ounces, they’re among the lightest premium noise-canceling headphones, with generously padded earcups and a cushioned headband that spreads pressure without gripping too tightly. They’re also easy to pack for travel, as the earcups fold and swivel for storage in the included hard-shell carrying case.

The Bose SoundLink Plus hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers,” and it’s down to $179 (originally $269). This is a great opportunity to snatch a quality portable speaker with a big discount.

Amazon has cut the price of its latest Fire TV Stick 4K, dropping it to $24.99 from $59.99 and bringing it to its lowest price ever. At this price, it's an affordable way to bring 4K streaming to an older television or give a sluggish smart TV a performance upgrade.

The Sony WH-CH730N are $128 (originally $179), the lowest price they've ever been. They use the same Sony Connect app as the premium headphones; as a result, you get a 10-band slider on the EQ menu, a battery care feature that extends the longevity of your battery life, 50 hours of juice, ANC, Ambient Sound (transparency mode), Multipoint to connect to two devices at once, and Bluetooth 6.0.

I got the Roborock Qrevo CurvX because it seemed like the perfect robot vacuum for me, as I have a dog, a mix of different floor types, and a gym with a workout mat, and it excels at handling them all. Amazon currently has it for $749.99 (originally $1,499.99), a 50% discount, and the lowest price it has ever been.

Samsung’s HW-Q600F soundbar is down to $379.97 at Amazon from $499.99, a $110 discount that brings it to its lowest price ever. This 2025 model sits in the middle of Samsung’s Q-Series lineup and pairs a sleek, angular bar with a subwoofer in a 3.1.2 setup. Dolby Atmos also brings a modest sense of height, and effects track cleanly from left to right. You get a graphic equalizer and sound presets for adjusting the audio to your preferences through the included remote.

The Ultimate Ears Miniroll is down to $49.99 (originally $79.99), the second-lowest it has sold for so far. It’s a small, flat, puck-shaped Bluetooth speaker that weighs just over half a pound, with a removable rubber strap you can attach to a backpack, bike handlebar, or shower caddy. Despite its size, the Miniroll can get surprisingly loud—which PCMag confirms in its review—and at moderate volume, it has enough sound for a kitchen or backyard without sounding thin. As for its battery life, you get about 12 hours of playback before it needs a charge over USB-C, while its IP67 rating protects it from dust and a brief dunk in water.

If you're looking for a premium model, Samsung’s 65-inch S90H OLED TV is down to $1,397.99 from $2,697.99 at launch, saving you over $1,000. The sale price is easier to justify when you consider that this is a new 2026 model. If the 65-inch model does not suit your space, Samsung also sells the S90H in 42-, 48-, 55-, 77-, and 83-inch versions, and those sizes are discounted as well.

#3611. Slay the Spire 2 is one of this year's best selling games despite only being available on PC, and its players are "obsessed"

One million copies for each month on sale, it seems. Slay the Spire 2, Mega Crit's roguelike deckbuilder, is estimated to have sold 7.9m copies since its release in Steam Early Access in March.

That's according to estimates by Alinea Analytics industry analyst Rhys Elliott, who revealed in a LinkedIn post that those sales translate to $157.6m (~£119.6m) in revenue for the small studio.

Slay the Spire 2 is now the sixth best-selling 2026 release across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox. That is notable, as the game is only out on Steam, meaning it has sold enough copies to outpace games on platforms it's not even available on.

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. It quickly became March's top-selling game on Steam, beating blockbuster competition in Crimson Desert and Resident Evil Requiem. Slay the Spire 2, alongside other indie titles such as Meccha Chameleon, have helped Steam deliver another record year of revenue.

It was such a hit, even, that other indie developers felt it negatively impacted sales of their own games. Mewgenics maker Edmund McMillen recently told Eurogamer "it sucked everybody out". "The same players who liked Mewgenics, they were Slay The Spire players. So they all went woosh and right over," McMillen said.

Slay the Spire 2 has been consistently popular with players, too, and that popularity has seemingly continued. Elliott noted the game never fell below 2.5 million active players each month since March.

Slay the Spire 2's loyal following also meant that the recently released beta patch, which added a new character, was enough to bring back millions of players. Despite only being available for players who opt into the beta branch of the game, Slay the Spire 2 more than doubled its daily active users to reach its highest daily player count in six months.

"Simply put: Slay the Spire 2 players are obsessed," wrote Elliott. "And it's not just a niche group of dedicated players, either. The average play time is nearly 84 hours, sure. But zooming out, 1.9 million folks have played for over 100 hours."

Incidentally, nearly 100,000 players bought the game but never played it, which Elliott added could explain the discrepancy between player numbers and copies sold.

Looking ahead, Slay the Spire 2's road to version 1.0 is expected to be long, with several features and gameplay additions still in the works. Then there are the console ports, which have yet to be announced, but are very much expected.

In Eurogamer's Slay the Spire 2 early access review, Bertie Purchese called it "a deceptively familiar sequel" whose confident design and smart new additions build on what made the original work so well.

The newest Saturday Night Live episode aired last weekend, with comedian John Mulaney serving as Season 52’s latest host and Phoebe Bridgers performing as the musical guest. Unsurprisingly, the episode began with a cold open centered around recent events, and it centered on the controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. As part of that segment, Elon Musk was lampooned by the show again and, after he expressed disappointment with the impression, cast member Jeremy Culhane reacted.

SNL’s latest cold open sees the CIA gathering the U.S’ biggest tech magnates for a training session on not exposing secrets to potential operatives. The presiding official (played by Mulaney) speaks to Musk (Jeremy Culhane), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline) and Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson). After Mulaney’s character unsuccessfully tries to make his case, Huang (played by returning cast member Bowen Yang) warns his colleagues using his own experience.

Ultimately, the real Elon Musk appeared to be less than impressed with the sketch, in which Mulaney’s character used venn diagrams to explain to the CEOs that a woman wouldn’t truly be interested in them without an ulterior motive. In response, Musk dropped a comment under the sketch on X and included a diagram of his own:

@nbcsnl lol https://t.co/7vw3wS9Jm3November 16, 2026

Throughout the sketch, Culhane’s Musk makes several random statements at the fictional briefing, one of which sees him compare himself to James Bond and another in which he tries to connect with Huang over their leather jackets. It’s because of those random asides that both the CIA official and even Huang use spray bottles on Culhane’s Musk. On X, after someone ranked the performances the actual SpaceX founder shared his take on Culhane’s impression, writing:

I’d give them maybe 5/10 for me. They need to try harder.

This isn’t the first time Musk has taken issue with an impression of himself on Saturday Night Live. Back in late 2024, the tech mogul – who also hosted SNL in 2021 – called out Dana Carvey for his take on him. The following year would also see Musk chastise Mike Meyers’ impression of him as well. The Tesla figurehead is far from the only star to ever take issue with an impression, as Kanye West disliked Chris Redd’s impression of him Also, Ice Cube was dismissive of Kenan Thompson’s take on him.

After this latest Musk impression, Jeremy Culhane took to his Instagram story to share a headline about Musk’s reaction. The Sex Lives of College Girls alum simply added the following caption to his post:

Reading between the lines, Culhane’s response seems to be a bit of trolling on his part. He may not have gone into detail, but it’s easy to get the feeling that he’s not too perturbed by Musk’s reaction to his performance. On the night of the taping, the actor’s performance also generated considerable laughs from the live studio audience. As for whether Musk might feel compelled to issue a response to the comedian’s social media post, that remains to be seen.

What can probably be assumed at this point, however, is that as long as Elon Musk remains in the news, this probably won’t be the last time he’s parodied on the long-running sketch comedy show. Viewers will ultimately just have to wait and see if or how further sketches materialize and for what reason. On that note, check out Saturday Night Live when it airs on the titular night at 11:30 p.m. ET amid the 2026 TV schedule. Episodes are also available to stream with a Peacock subscription.

#3609. Three Ways to Avoid CAPTCHA Prompts When Using a VPN

VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins. When you borrow an IP address that hundreds of other people are also using for any number of reasons, you’re much more likely to get repeat verification requests from online firewalls.

CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam. They’re supposed to be easy for people but hard for robots, such as simple object recognition tasks or audio-visual challenges. However, they can still disrupt your browsing experience if they happen too frequently.

Most modern CAPTCHA providers, like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile, start working long before they give you a puzzle to solve. It usually starts with a risk score that studies your IP address, browser and device signals, or recent online activity.

If the CAPTCHA provider can’t confidently identify your request as human based on those signals, it requests that you complete a puzzle before deciding if the request should be blocked. That means when you get repeat CAPTCHA requests, there’s something affecting your browser’s risk score. For example, popular VPN servers spread the same IP address across any number of users, which can easily make a website mistake you for a bot farm. If you change your IP address frequently by switching servers often, that might look suspicious too.

Luckily, there are ways to deal with frequent CAPTCHA requests using tools and services available with your browser and VPN. Cloudflare has already cut its CAPTCHA requests by 91% using its Managed Challenge platform. Apple has also been shipping token-based verification on devices since iOS 16 and macOS Ventura. In June 2026, Cloudflare even announced a joint effort called the Private Access Control Tokens (PACT) standard with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Shopify.

While there’s no direct off switch for CAPTCHAs, you can use different fixes to improve your browser’s trust signals when using the internet. That way, you’re less likely to be hounded by verification requests.

The easiest fix for repeat CAPTCHAs is to stop connecting to whichever server your VPN app picks automatically. Proton recommends choosing servers with lower traffic load. In fact, its apps display load as a percentage to help you avoid the most crowded options. I'd also skip big traffic hubs like New York or London, since that's where most traffic originates from. Servers in smaller cities located nearby are often just as fast but never as populated.

You should also avoid changing IP addresses too frequently, which can look suspicious on its own. Pick a server that seems to behave well, then continue using it for at least one session. Also remember you’re more likely to get premium server options if you’re on a paid VPN plan. Major platforms like ExpressVPN, Surfshark, Proton, and Nord are particularly likely to have a larger server collection to pick from.

Costs nothing more than your current subscription

Hopping between servers often can backfire

Private Access Tokens (PAT) let you verify the authenticity of your request using your device rather than an IP address. Apple calls it Automatic Verification, where an Apple server validates your device and Apple Account to assign you an anonymous token.

To enable Automatic Verification on an iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification. On a Mac, open System Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification.

Unfortunately, there’s no equivalent feature for Windows, Android, and Linux users. That said, Cloudflare offers the Silk extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that serves a similar function. A quick look at the ratings will tell you it’s not as effective, but Cloudflare’s upcoming cross-browser standard called PACT seems promising once it is released.

Doesn’t share personal details with websites

Chrome and Firefox extensions can be unreliable

If you pay a bit extra for a dedicated IP add-on, VPN providers can assign you a unique IP address that isn’t shared with anyone else. For example, NordVPN offers dedicated IPs in 30 countries for $2-5 a month and Surfshark charges $3.75 a month for it.

There are also dedicated providers like Private Internet Access, which charges $3.99 per month for a zero-trust setup so not even their employees know which IP address is assigned to you. On the other hand, Proton VPN offers dedicated IPs only to business plan users, so you’ll need to be on the Workspace Standard, Premium, or Enterprise plans to get one.

That said, there is a trade-off here too. NordVPN itself admits that a dedicated IP makes it easier to link online activity back to a single user. Also, many websites can still tell that the IP address originated from a VPN data center rather than a consumer’s device.

Get unique IP addresses with pristine reputation

Works across desktop, mobile, and even smart TVs

Also functions as an allowlisted address for work

Add-ons cost more on top of the VPN subscription

Offers less anonymity than shared VPN servers

#3608. Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"

Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year. In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.

"No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."

Her motivation for this initiative? Simply, she wants to change how the industry works. "I've discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it's a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations."

"The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help," she added later. "That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don't know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry."

Sandfall Interactive previously said its guiding "North Star" will always be its "own personal taste", and what the team enjoys.She noted that she didn't think the studio would bow to pressure from fans to do more of the same, but instead be guided by what it thinks is best for itself, and for the series. "I've seen too many TV shows and books be swayed trying to please a lot of people, and in the process you end up losing the heart of what's there," she noted.

We know that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is "not the end" of the franchise, and it seems that whatever happens next, it'll have at least a little bit of Svedberg-Yen's creativity instilled in it. I wish her the best for whatever her next step is.
