#3578. Andrew Scott On What Makes Elsinore “So Moving”

Although the emotional core of Elsinore is centered around beloved actor Ian Charleston dealing with terminal illness, its star Andrew Scott says the film has as much heart as it does humor.

“The most singular thing about our film I think is the humor in it,” he said during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “The tragedy in some ways is a little bit like Hamlet itself, but you can't make a film about Ian Charleston without having gags in it. He was incredibly funny. Every person [who knew him] said he was just wickedly funny, and flirtatious, and he was always looking towards the light, and he had a certain degree of courage. So that is something I think that we all share as a sense of humor.”

Andrew Scott, Billie Piper, Stephen Beresford and Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Elsinore tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS. Scott has received early acclaim for his powerful portrayal of Charleson. Before the film began Vanity Fair’s West Coast Editor John Ross warned the audience that "first you're going to laugh, then you're going to cry," while watching Scott’s performance.

“I think … why the film is so moving is because [Charleson’s] not wallowing at any point. He was insanely courageous,” continued Scott. “So that to me was the thing that we were the most

insistent on in some ways. And that's really all down to finding actors who in this extraordinary ensemble have a really terrific sense of humor. And we kind of knew that we could, with the screenplay, get the best actors in the country. And I feel we did.”

The panel conversation featured Scott, costar Billie Piper, and writer Stephen Beresford, moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford, following an exclusive screening of the film.

Billie Piper at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Piper, who plays Charleston's close friend Patsy, she relied heavily on Beresford's script for her prep, as well as information she gleaned from those who actually knew Patsy, and Charleston.

“I've spoken to a few members of the family, their friends, and then I sort of cherry-picked things from people I'd known in the beginning of my career, the louder figures in our industry,” she said. “And then I did my own interpretation and just had a good time. It's a very moving story, but I had a lot of fun playing that part. She's a really joyful character to play, I enjoyed the comedy. And I understand that a lot of her jokes are coming from a place of despair.”

Beresford, who has known Scott for 25 years, said he didn't initially think of his longtime friend for the role, but should have.

“The story of Ian, and Ian's Hamlet [performance] is legendary in the British theater,” he said. “So many people said it was the greatest Hamlet they'd ever seen, and that it had this incredible quality. So I knew about the story, and then it was brought to me actually as an idea by a producer who said, ‘What about writing about Ian Charleston, and what about Andrew playing Ian Charleston?’ And then I just thought, ‘Well, why didn't I have that idea myself five years ago?’ So yeah, that's really how it happened, and I started to research it, the details of the story were so incredible, and so moving.”

Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Scott, who famously played Hamlet onstage 150 times beginning in 2017, prior to filming Elsinore, closed out the panel conversation by reciting his favorite line from the classic tragedy.

“When Hamlet says the line about the war that was going on—and this was written 400 years ago—it just seems so relevant to what he might have been experiencing at the time, which is: ‘I see the imminent death of 20,000 men who for a fantasy, a trick of fame, go to their graves like beds.’ The idea that that was written 400 years ago, and that he was watching 50 percent of his friends die for no reason and be neglected by governments, and derided by the public. And it was just happening, and happening time and time again.”

Scott continued: “The reason that I love it so much is that when I was doing Hamlet myself, of course I wasn't thinking about the AIDS crisis, but the enduring nature of art, something that was written 400 years ago by Shakespeare, could actually be of use to somebody in 1989 and then be reproduced again in 2026 and be of use. And that idea of art being useful down the lines is so moving to me.”

Vanity Fair's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, Elsinore stars Andrew Scott and Billie Piper and writer Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3576. Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Breaks His Silence, Says He Would Come Back

Jensen Huang, the co-founder of Nvidia who was recently ousted as CEO after he admitted to having an affair with someone that US intelligence believes could by a spy for China, has now said he is open to returning to the company.

In his first public statement since his resignation from Nvidia, Huang told The Wall Street Journal that he is aware of the "outpouring of calls" from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners, and customers for him to come back as CEO. He would come back, if asked.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," he said.

This statement came a day after a source told CNBC that the Nvidia board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO.

Huang released his statement on social media, saying, "Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me."

His statement added: "I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia."

Huang acknowledged that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia" and owned up to making "serious mistakes in my personal life." He said he created problems for Nvidia's Board of Directors and he said he "deeply" regrets that. "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he said.

Nvidia was the world's biggest company by market cap until the company's stock price began to crash in October, and it fell further after the controversies came to light, including multiple affairs beyond the one with the alleged spy.

To be sure, Nvidia remains a juggernaut--it's currently the No. 2 biggest company in the world, with a market cap of $3.75 trillion. Only Apple, with a market cap above $4 trillion, is bigger than Nvidia.

The New York Times and other media outlets reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with the former CEO of the AI company Megaspeed, Alice Huang (no relation). US intelligence sources claim that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, though China officially denies this narrative and says it's an effort by the US to smear China.

Megaspeed, for its part, said Alice Huang left the company in 2025 and denied any wrongdoing in the Nvidia scandal.

The Nvidia controversies have led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the "Mag 7" companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia's accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade. Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke.

Nvidia's interim boss is CFO Colette Kress, who is expected to lead Nvidia's earnings call today, November 17. The earnings report will be closely watched and highly scrutinized--keep checking back with GameSpot for the latest.

Maura Higgins became a quick fan favorite on Dancing with the Stars, but I'm worried she could miss the Season 35 finals. With the semifinals and one vote before the finale, I'm afraid her run on the 2026 TV schedule may be at an end. Now, it seems I may have more reason to be concerned about what lies ahead.

On the heels of a tough Grammy night featuring the "Thong Song," it was clear Higgins' rib injury was more than a storyline for DWTS to play up. Now, per a new rumor from The Sun, Higgins allegedly had to cancel a rehearsal and seek medical attention while preparing for Dancing with the Stars' semifinals. Her rib was reportedly re-injured over the weekend, leaving some questions about how she'll be able to perform during the live episode.

As viewers learned in last week's episode, Higgins didn't break her rib, but the swelling and damage caused so much pain that she briefly considered throwing in the towel. It'd be a shame to see, given just how far she's come since the beginning, but obviously, her health takes priority.

As of late, I've written about how Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik's advancement could set up a fan favorite going home instead of them on Semifinals night. Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas were on my shortlist of people who could go home, and honestly, I think it's all going to come down to who gives the best performance.

I Thought I Knew Who I Wanted To Win DWTS Season 35. But One Comment Totally Changed My Opinion

One can never rule out the impact of fans, however, and I do wonder how this rumor could impact their thoughts on whether she should advance. Part of me thinks she could gain sympathy, assuming she wants to keep going, and get the pass to have another week to recover, give it her all, and try to win DWTS on finale night.

Conversely, I could see some viewers deciding it's her time if the performance is weak or if it's evident that she's struggling with an injury. I would see sending her home as more of an act of mercy at that point, rather than putting the pressure on her to drop out of the finale.

All this to say, I'll have all eyes on Maura Higgins as the DWTS semifinals play out. There's so much chatter happening online about who could go home, and this situation is just another layer to consider. I even think there's a possibility that Harry Shum Jr. could miss the finale, which makes the prospect of this episode so much wilder.

Dancing With The Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. This is going to be the biggest episode of the season thus far, so make sure to clear that primetime schedule to see what happens!

#3574. All The Game Awards 2026 Nominees Revealed

It's almost time for The Game Awards to kick off a night of trailers and appreciation for the 2026 gaming year, but right now, it's time to see who's in the running to earn some well-deserved kudos. The 2026 Game Awards will be livestreamed from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on December 10, and nominees for the best games across several categories have been announced.

Like previous years, the nominees have been chosen by a global jury of media publications and creator outlets--including GameSpot--and were announced through a dedicated livestream.

Leading the nominations is Grand Theft Auto 6 with eight nominations, Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem with six nominations each, and Phantom Blade Zero has earned an impressive five nominations. Big Walk, 007 First Light, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake have also earned plenty of nods, with four nominations each.

Here's a closer look at which games are in the running for several of the biggest prizes at The Game Awards this year.

Game of the Year

The best of the best for 2026, the game that excelled across multiple creative and technical fields.

  • Control Resonant
  • Grand Theft Auto 6
  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Resident Evil Requiem
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

For the game that was built with an outstanding creative vision and executed it through polished direction and design.

  • Grand Theft Auto 6
  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Pragmata
  • Resident Evil Requiem

  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

#3573. Who Is Anne Hathaway's Husband? Meet Adam Shulman Amid Baby No. 3's Arrival

Anne Hathaway has millions of fans thanks to her expansive acting catalog, but her husband, Adam Shulman, has always felt like home.

“I knew from the second I met him that he was the love of my life,” Hathaway told Harper’s Bazaar UK in February 2013, less than one year after they got married.

The Princess Diaries star recalled telling a mutual friend of theirs, “I’m going to marry that man,” soon after they first crossed paths. “I think he thought I was a little nuts, which I am a bit, but I’m also nice,” she teased.

Hathaway — who announced in June 2026 that she is expecting her third baby with Shulman — isn’t the only one who is happy she met her match in the jewelry designer.

Her Devil Wears Prada 2 costar Emily Blunt told Elle in March 2017 that Shulman “has been Annie’s greatest achievement in many ways. He’s sort of home away from the storm of fame that she lives with.”

Blunt gushed, “Being with the right person has been a major part of her growth, but I don’t think she cares as much anymore. That’s something both of us feel now: Who f***ing cares? You get to a point where the stuff that you used to sweat just doesn’t matter. It’s a great place to be.”

Scroll down to learn more about Hathaway’s husband:

After growing up in New York, Shulman attended Brown University. He graduated in 2003 with a bachelor’s of arts in theater.

Shulman is a man of many talents, one of which is working as a jewelry designer. His brand is called James Banks Design, which according to its website makes handmade pieces from recycled materials in Southern California.

Shulman’s greatest work might be designing Hathaway’s emerald-shaped diamond engagement ring, which he proposed with in November 2011. In September 2024, Shulman released a Butterfly Bag red handbag in collaboration with Peter Nitz, and Hathaway was one of the first to celebrate.

“Proud wife alert: I thought you all might like to know that Adam aka @jamesbanksdesign has some new work out,” she wrote via Instagram at the time.

Shulman had a five-episode arc on American Dreams in 2005, playing Paul O’Bannon. He made a cameo on The West Wing one year later before starring in 2007’s The Dukes of Hazzard: The Beginning TV movie. Shulman can also be seen in 2008’s The Gold Lunch short film and 2015’s Ricki and the Flash as a Total Foods customer.

Shulman met Hathaway at the Palm Spring Film Festival in April 2008, and they began dating that November. The pair got engaged in November 2011, tying the knot in September 2012.

The couple exchanged vows in Big Sur, California, surrounded by family and friends.

In addition to being in front of the camera from time to time, Shulman has worked behind the scenes alongside his wife. The pair first collaborated on 2014’s Song One, an indie drama film in which Hathaway played Franny.

“At first, I was curious how it would go. People always say don’t work with your spouse. But I loved working with him,” Hathaway told People at the time of partnering with Shulman. “He’s really good at this, and he’s a wonderful producer. And I feel like I actually learned a lot from him in the process.”

Shulman is set to work as an executive producer on the upcoming series Fear Not, which is in pre-production, according to IMDB.

The Devil Wears Prada actress welcomed her first child with Shulman, son Jonathan, in March 2016.

“As was to be expected, he is spectacular,” Hathaway told Entertainment Tonight of her husband’s parenting two months after she gave birth.

The couple welcomed their second child, son Jack, in November 2019.

Hathaway announced in June 2026 that she is pregnant with her and Shulman’s third baby. “x Baby I’m yours x,” she captioned an Instagram video, showing off her baby bump.

In November 2026, Hathaway was spotted in New York City with a newborn baby strapped to her chest in a carrier. Us reached out to a rep for the actress for comment.

The Oscar winner revealed during a 2023 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show that she and Shulman have matching ink.

“We have this thing, it’s actually a tattoo, and the idea is that individually we’re whole, but together we’re more,” Hathaway explained, revealing the letter “M” tattooed on her left wrist. “And so I think it’s just that thing [where] I don’t expect him to complete me and he doesn’t expect me to complete him.”

She added, “I’m my own person. He’s his own person and we choose to be together because we believe we make each other better. And this union is something we both want to participate in.”

#3572. Hillary Clinton Showed Up For Dinner at Gloria Steinem’s Townhouse

It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election. “One of my most anticipated moments will be watching Donald Trump walk into the State of the Union through the now more than one hundred women members of the House of Representatives. I just want them all to stare at him and say, ‘You fired us from jobs we were qualified for. You insulted us. You demeaned our ambition. You undermined our place in government and society. And we’re here.’”

Huma Abedin, Busy Philips, and Paloma Elsesser.

The former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist. She passed away in September, but the feminist pathfinder was known for throwing these salon-type events (she called them “circles”) at her Upper East Side townhouse, which she bought for just $30,000 in the late ’60s. It’s overflowing with books (I spy Marilyn by Norman Mailer, Jane Fonda’s War by Mary Hershberger, and several Eleanor Roosevelt biographies on the shelves), pictures (there’s one framed of Steinem alongside Mariska Hargitay) and Indian art. (Steinem spent two formative years in the country.) There are magnets in her kitchen of Wonder Woman, Frida Kahlo, and a cloth finger puppet of Hillary Clinton. A political button is pinned to it that says “Another Bitch for Hillary.” The whole place smells like a Cire Trudon candle, and everyone’s drinking negronis. (Which actually isn’t technically very Steinem—her favorite cocktail was a margarita—but the negronis go with the night’s dinner, prepared by Lilia chef Missy Robbins.) Yet this is one of the first events at the townhouse that Steinem herself isn’t here to lead.

Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.

Amy Richards, a feminist activist whom many consider to be the daughter Steinem never had—a title Richards rejects because her mentor “didn’t want kids”—stood up at one point to tell the crowd that this is what Steinem would have wanted. Growing up with a transient father and a mentally volatile mother, the late activist took near-obsessive care in maintaining a welcoming home she could share with others. “As long as I knew Gloria, she always said, ‘I just want my home to be the way it’s always been.’ She wanted it to be filled with people,” Richards says. “She didn’t grow up with a home. She was traveling the country for the first 10 years of her life and then lived with her mother, who was not very stable.”

At least Steinem’s still here on the wall: Months before her death, she posed for a series of portraits by Paola Kudacki for Weldun, a platform that offers physically adaptive and functional fashion. It was a bit of a small miracle that Steinem said yes. “I will say, Gloria did not always love to be photographed,” Richards says. “Especially in her later years—not because of wrinkles or aging, but she was just like, ‘Aren’t there enough pictures of me?’” Weldun and the Gloria Steinem Foundation are presenting tonight’s dinner, and mementos of Steinem are everywhere. On the fireplace mantle sits a pair of her signature Ray-Ban aviators. But Gloria’s stuff isn’t the same as Gloria herself.

Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton hugging Melissa McCarthy.

Which is probably why, in a crowd of women that include Huma Abedin, Mariska Hargitay, Padma Lakshmi, Melissa McCarthy, and Bethann Hardison—who, at the ripe age of 84, shows up wearing Gucci—Clinton’s unexpected arrival feels seismic, like Gloria sent someone in her place. (Hardison tells me she thinks Steinem used whatever divine power she’s got up there to launch the Blue Wave: “She’s probably saying she helped it happen!”) Whatever your views on Clinton’s politics, she was the first woman to receive a presidential nomination from a major party. Paloma Elsesser and I sit crouched in a corner of the room, glued to the window. “There’s mother,” the supermodel whispers to me as Clinton exits her car into the pouring rain and walks up to the townhouse door.

Guests at dinner honoring the late Gloria Steinem.

“Hi, everybody,” Clinton says as she walks in. The entire dinner comes to a silent halt. “Hi,” the room responds in unison. Madame Secretary doesn’t seem to like the fuss, probably because 30 or so people intensely staring at you when you arrive at a party is objectively unsettling. “Go back to eating!” she says, motioning to the Missy Robbins meal on the table. Clinton sits down next to Naomi Watts and warmly greets Busy Philips, who stumped for Clinton back in 2016. Hargitay blows her a kiss across the table. All anyone wants to do is talk to Clinton about the 2026 election, in which Democrats won at least 55 seats in the Senate and 256 in the House to take both majorities in the US Congress. At the end of the meal—and after a proper catch-up with Shonda Rhimes—Clinton tries to leave, but she can’t. Guests block the door, clamoring to chat her up.

Amid the Clinton traffic jam, I ask Hargitay about the photo. She can’t remember exactly what it is from. “Was it Bravo? Was it with Andy…what’s his name?” But she can guess what she thinks Steinem might say about the blue wave: “There is a God!”

I watch Clinton finally make her exit. It’s late, so I wait several minutes before I descend the stairs to leave too. (I wait for Elsesser, Watts, Hardinn, and Lux Pascal to finish taking a selfie on the steps.) But I spoke too soon: Clinton’s stuck waiting for the coat check, another group of women crowded around her hoping to say something—or, more likely, hoping she says something. With the way this night is going, Clinton might be the last one at the party.

#3571. Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November

The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month--and eight games will also be leaving Game Pass on November 30.

Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet.

The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs.

Other highlights this month include Call of the Elder Gods for a Lovecraftian puzzle-adventure, High on Life 2 joining Game Pass Premium, and Roadside Research, which is all about aliens trying to run a gas station while poorly disguised as humans.

If you're looking for action, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is worth checking out. All the thrill of long-distance sniping, with a surprising amount of close-quarters stealth gameplay as well. Also recommended is Motorslice, where you'll get to parkour through the ruins of a brutalist megastructure, climb massive bosses in tense fights, and hunt down living construction equipment.

Starting in December, you can get Freestyle Football 2, which is an online multiplayer soccer game built around 5v5 matches. We already have that game in the form of Rematch from Sifu developer Sloclap, but if you want a different spin on that soccer idea, take a quick look.

Xbox Game Pass November Wave 2 Games

November 17

  • Paw Patrol: Dino World (Xbox Series X|S, PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

November 18

  • Call of the Elder Gods (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • High on Life 2 (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Roadside Research (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC via Game Preview -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass

November 19

  • Black Jacket (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass

November 24

  • Motorslice (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

November 27

  • Arkheron (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Game Preview) -- Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

December 1

  • The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

December 3

  • Freestyle Football 2 (Xbox Series X|S, PC)

November has been pretty good for new entries in the Game Pass library, with the start of the month bringing the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, while subscribers also got Void/Breaker, Warhammer Survivors, and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. Game Pass Essential saw a big influx of new games, with several Banjo-Kazooie titles joining People Can Fly’s Gears of War prequel and the beloved Viva Piñata games.

#3570. GTA 6’s Lucia Actor Revealed, And It’s The Person Everyone Already Guessed

The actor playing Lucia in Grand Theft Auto 6 has been revealed, and it's Manni L. Perez, the person everyone expected it to be for a long time now. In fact, fans discovered that Perez was Lucia all the way back in 2023.

The news didn't come from Rockstar Games or the actor herself, but instead via The Game Awards. That's because Perez was nominated for Best Performance. GTA 6, meanwhile, was nominated for overall Game of the Year this year, and that's sorta awkward because reviews for the game aren't live yet.

Perez was nominated for Best Performance alongside Patrick Gibson (007 First Light), Angela Sant'Albano (Resident Evil Requiem), Liam McIntyre (Marvel's Wolverine), and Rahul Kohli (Saros). The actor playing Jason in GTA 6 remains a mystery, but people widely believe it's Dylan Rourke.

GTA 6 leads the way this year at The Game Awards with eight nominations. These include:

  • Game of the Year
  • Best Game DIrection
  • Best Narrative
  • Best Art Direction
  • Best Score and Music
  • Best Audio Design
  • Best Performance (Manni L. Perez)
  • Best Action/Adventure Game

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC release reportedly on tap for early 2027.

In addition to Perez as Lucia and someone else as Jason, we've learned that veteran actor Stephen Root will play Brian Heder. People believe Saturday Night Live actor Bobby Moynihan is playing Cal Hampton, but this is not confirmed yet. For more, check out all the GTA 6 confirmed and rumored actors.

#3569. The Bachelor’s Peter Weber and Jadeyn Carr’s Relationship Timeline

Former Bachelor Peter Weber has found love with model Jadeyn Carr.

In a matter of months, the pilot subtly debuted his newfound romance via social media, announced they had twins on the way and popped the question.

Weber, who first appeared in Bachelor Nation in 2019 as a contestant on Hannah Brown‘s season 15 of The Bachelorette and later led season 24 of The Bachelor in 2020, had been linked to former contestant Kelley Flanagan, former show producer Julie LaPlaca and actress Brook Sill before meeting Carr online.

Keep scrolling for Weber and Carr’s full relationship timeline:

Weber confirmed his romance with Carr via Instagram, in which the model joined her beau on a family trip to the Adirondacks in upstate New York.

“Summer ’26,” Weber captioned his upload, which did not mention Carr by name.

Less than a week later, Weber shared a second post with Carr. “Favorites,” he wrote photos of his then-girlfriend joining him in a plane’s cockpit and cuddling on a beach vacation.

Bachelor Nation members quickly flooded the comments. “The hard launch finally 👏,” Luke Stone wrote, while Clay Harbor chimed in with a trio of clapping emojis.

Weber’s family embraced Carr publicly, too. His mother, Barbara, shared a photo of the couple to her own Instagram with the caption, “SO HAPPY YOU BROUGHT HER HOME!!❤️ … I’m so happy for you two! She fits into all of our hearts❤️.”

Weber’s brother, Jack, left his own note on the couple’s early posts, writing “Love this ❤️.”.

Just weeks after going Instagram official, Weber and Carr revealed a major surprise.

“1 + 1 = 4 ♥️,” they wrote in the joint caption, alongside images of Weber kissing Carr’s bare baby bump.

Weber’s family celebrated the news in the comments. “Wohoo! Can’t wait to meet them!!” Jack wrote, while Barbara added, “Gods sweetest blessings! So So loved already!! You two will be the best parents!! Love you 4!❤️❤️❤️❤️.”

Weber announced on November 11 that he proposed to Carr in New York City’s Central Park.

“Marry Me @jadeyncarr,” he captioned a carousel of photos from the proposal, in which he presented Carr with an oval diamond engagement ring.

Less than one week later, Weber confirmed he had married Carr.

“I was debating if I should reveal this here, but you guys have all been here following my journey for a very long time,” Peter said during Bachelor Nation’s Vacation at Sea on November 17. “I can officially say that on 11/11, I married the love of my life.”

Back in August, the public was devastated to learn that actress Hayden Panettiere died at age 36. This was a huge shock, especially considering her brother died just a few years earlier. Fans are still mourning and re-watching her work on projects like Heroes, and plenty of people were surprised when Panettiere's mother Lesley Vogel didn't attend her celebration of life back in September. Now Vogel is speaking out and explaining her absence for the services.

Fans still have questions about Hayden Panettiere's death, and were curious about why her mother wasn't in attendance for the late actress' funeral services. Lesley Vogel recently appeared on Inside Edition, where she explained why she chose to opt out of her daughter's celebration of life. She was quoted saying:

I just didn’t want to rock the boat either; it was probably for the best.

During the interview, she shared that she and Hayden Panettiere drifted away from each other after the Scream actress' relationship with ex Brian Hickerson started picking up. They mother and daughter seemingly had a difficult relationship, some of which was mentioned in the actress' memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning. Still, it was surprising for some that Vogel didn't attend the funeral services.

While appearing in the same interview, Lesley Vogel claimed that she was indeed invited, but didn't think her presence would be helpful during this difficult time. She went on to say:

I knew that some of the people there wanted to believe I was the horrible mother because Hayden was angry and made statements.

Clearly this was a complicated situation, which might explain why Hayden Panettiere's mother ultimately decided not to attend her funeral. She knew there'd be discourse about her either way, but is seemingly at peace with her decision. Inside Edition contacted Brian Hickerson for a comment, but did not hear back from him.

Panettiere's death hit the public hard, largely because she grew up right in front of our eyes, including early roles in projects like Remember the Titans and A Bug's Life. Millennial fans in particular grew up alongside her, and there was a ton of love her work on Ice Princess, Heroes, Nashville, and the Scream movies (the latter of which are streaming with a Paramount+ subscription). Folks were thrilled when she reprised her role as Kirby Reed in Scream VI, with Panettiere thanking fans who "came to her rescue". Clearly she's someone who meant a great deal to her fans, many of whom are still processing her death. As for Lesley Vogel, she's given an explanation for missing her late daughter's funeral.

Hayden Panettiere's legacy lives on through her various acting credits. Heroes is streaming on Netflix, while Nashville is over on Pluto TV. Our thoughts continue to be with her loved ones as they mourn and grapple with the loss.

Apple announced a slew of products in March, including the MacBook Air with the M5 chip, which ended up increasing in price in June due to the RAM shortage. These MacBooks come in both 13-inch and 15-inch sizes, and if you're interested in either, it's a good time to buy: In the leadup to Black Friday, Amazon is selling both at a $200 discount, and the 1 TB storage versions for $250 off.

The M5 MacBook Air is the best laptop for most people looking for a new machine in 2026. In comparison to the already excellent M4 Airs, the M5 base model has double the storage at 512GB. #3566. Avril Lavigne Welcomes Her First Child At Age 42

Avril Lavigne is now a mom. The 42-year-old Canadian might count songs like "Here's to Never Growing Up" among her hits, but in news posted to Instagram Friday, Avril Lavigne revealed a very grown-up milestone.

Beneath a carousel of three black-and-white photos, Lavigne wrote “Our Mini Fucking Princess has arrived,” followed by emojis depicting a baby bottle, a crown, and a pink heart and bow. One photo shows Lavigne cradling an infant dressed in an animal-print onesie and matching headband, while another shows three pairs of Vans on a skateboard. No other details, including information on the baby's name or if Lavigne has a co-parent, were provided.

Avril Lavigne at the Viper Room in the early 2000s.

A spokesperson for the singer told People that “Avril has been enjoying time with her family while working on her new album and wants to thank the fans for all of their love!”

Lavigne has been married twice: once to Canadian guitarist Deryck Whibley and then to Chad Kroeger, the Canadian frontman of the band Nickelback. That latter partnership ended in 2018, but in 2022 she almost tied the knot a third time, with rapper Mod Sun. That relationship ended in 2023.

Mod Sun and Avril Lavigne attend the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards on August 28, 2022

One constant in Lavigne's life has been strong bond she shares with her parents. When, in May 2025, she brought her mother on stage at Madison Square Garden, she wrote on social media: “Ever since I was a little girl, both my mom and dad saw something in me and encouraged me to practice very hard and pursue my dream of becoming a singer/ musician. They made a lot of sacrifices for me and I could not be where I am today without them.”

Continuing, she wrote, “I am grateful to both my parents. Thank you for everything, I love you both!”

Lavigne was still a teenager when her parents allowed her to leave high school to pursue her dream, and her debut at age 17 was a smash hit. Her success continued with singles including 2002's chart-topper “Complicated" and 2021 song “Bite Me.”

Though Friday's announcement was a surprise to most, Lavigne has never been quiet about her desire to become a mom when the time is right. Speaking with E! News in 2013, she laid out her plan: "I want one or two [kids], but not right now," the then-29-year old said. "Like, in the future. Eventually."

#3565. GTA 6 Leads TGA Nominations, And Reviews Aren’t Even Live Yet

The Keighleys, or more formally, The Game Awards, are right around the corner. Ahead of its December 10 air date, host Geoff Keighley announced the nominees for the myriad categories, including Game of the Year. Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 made the cut, but in an unusual circumstance, it did so before any reviews of the game have been published.

Before anyone has read any official take on GTA 6, Rockstar Games' action-adventure game has eight nominations, making it the most-nominated game at this year's The Game Awards.

On top of being spotlighted for Game of the Year, the game also has nominations for Best Art Direction, Best Audio Design, Best Game Direction, Best Action/Adventure, Best Narrative, Best Performance (for Manni L. Perez's portrayal of Lucia), and Best Score, bringing the crime sim's total nominations to eight.

We already knew GTA 6 would be eligible for this year's ceremony. After all, per the TGA FAQ, the cutoff date for eligibility is November 20, one day after the game comes out. With a "jury of over 100 global media and influencer outlets" selecting the nominees, and many of these folks likely having plenty of hands-on time with Rockstar Games' latest release, it isn't much of a shocker to see GTA 6 at the top spot. Still, it is a little awkward that it has so many nominations before its release that may reveal what to expect from the critical reception..

Maybe it shouldn't be too surprising or weird, though. After all, the game isn't officially out yet, and it's already sold approximately 16 million copies and generated nearly $2 billion in revenue. Maybe that expensive sick day caused by the GTA Flu won't be so expensive.

#3564. Los Javis Are “Living a Dream” As La Bola Negra with Penélope Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente, and Miguel Bernardeau Collects Honors

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

“You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”

La Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo said they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she said, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician said he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

“I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”

Miguel Bernardeau at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3563. What Does It Take For World Of Warcraft To Be Nominated At The Game Awards?

The nominees for 2026's The Game Awards have been revealed, and just like every year before it, there is a glaring omission in the Best Ongoing Game Category: World of Warcraft.

This year's nominees are Arc Raiders, Fortnite, No Man's Sky, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Final Fantasy 14 Online. Of particular note is Square Enix's MMORPG, which has been nominated in the category every year since 2021. Developer Blizzard's MMO, on the other hand, is nowhere to be seen. 

WoW is among the most popular live-service games in industry history and has been for 22 years. Blizzard releases new expansions for its MMORPG every other year like clockwork and has done so for over two decades. It reintroduced the old-school version of the MMO, WoW Classic, in 2019 to huge acclaim from the game's passionate community.

In the years that followed, it continued to add new expansions to the modern version of WoW, adding highly requested features like account-wide unlocks and new endgame solo content. For WoW Classic, it re-released past expansions, added official servers and support for a permadeath mode popular among the game's community, and ran experimental seasons that added new content to the classic version of the game. Taken all together, the various versions of WoW have millions of players.

Earlier this year, Blizzard released Midnight, the latest expansion for modern WoW that added player housing to the MMO for the first time. A few weeks ago, it released WoW: Forever, the third major version of the MMO. Built on the bones of WoW Classic, Forever is intended to be an ongoing game that will add new content and changes to the old-school version of WoW, existing alongside the modern game. Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent players, Blizzard said.

Yet, since 2017, WoW has never even been nominated in Best Ongoing Game, a category that serves to put a spotlight on titles that continue to receive new content and evolve the experience over time--something Blizzard wrote the book on with WoW.

WoW being omitted this year in particular is more baffling than any time before, as Blizzard not only released a brand-new expansion, but also an entirely new version of the game that players have dreamed about for years. On the other hand, Final Fantasy 14's new expansion, Evercold, doesn't release until 2027, even if the game has received significant content updates over the course of the year. 

Even other Blizzard games have been nominated in this category multiple times over the years. Overwatch won Best Ongoing Game in 2017 and was nominated again in 2018. Diablo 4 earned a nomination in 2024 with the release of its first expansion, Vessel of Hatred. 

Meanwhile, it seems like nothing WoW does is enough to warrant attention. There is, of course, a simple answer to why this seems to be the case--nobody, or at least very few, on the The Game Awards voting jury plays, or keeps up to date, with WoW.

That's a shame, because if there was any year where WoW deserved to be nominated, it's this year. Forever is the culmination of an entire community's dream of having an ongoing, new version of classic WoW, and Midnight continues the philosophy of player-friendly changes first added in 2024's The War Within expansion. There are now more ways to play WoW than ever before, each receiving unprecedented support and updates. In fact, players in the modern version of WoW have been complaining that there's perhaps too much to do and that content updates are maybe too frequent. 

This is all to say that it feels like WoW deserves just a little recognition. It's been running for over two decades at this point, and in that time has in many ways defined what an "ongoing game" is and can be. 2026 has been a banner year for WoW, and its future is looking brighter than ever. It deserved a moment in the spotlight. Maybe next year (though I wouldn't bet on it).

Days before Christmas 2019, Catherine gave birth to their first daughter, Mia. “I’ve always wanted a daddy’s girl and now I’ve got her. Mia is healthy, Mama is doing great, and God is so good!” Sean wrote on December 23 via Instagram.

Juan Pablo Galavis opted not to propose to Nikki Ferrell during the season 18 finale of The Bachelor, but the duo continued to see each other for several months in 2014. After they called it quits that October, the former soccer player, who has a daughter named Camila from a previous relationship, married Osmariel Villalobos in August 2017. In March 2020, however, the Venezuelan model revealed the twosome had quietly split after two years of marriage.  “I want to close this chapter of my life in the same way it began, with LOVE, because even though I didn’t have a fairy tale, Juan Pablo tried to make me happy and I [tried to] make him happy … and in reality that is most important. You deserve this clarification, and so here it is. We are divorced,” she said via Instagram. “I believe that thanks to my past I am the person of the present (much more mature and with more experience).”

Farmer Chris Soules proposed to Whitney Bischoff during the season 19 finale of The Bachelor in 2015. Months after the finale aired, the twosome ended their engagement. Chris faced legal trouble in April 2017 after he was involved in a car crash that resulted in a man’s death. In November 2018, the former Dancing With the Stars contestant pleaded guilty to a charge related to the incident.  In May 2019, he was ordered to pay $2.5 million in the wrongful death lawsuit. Three months later, news broke that Chris agreed to a two-year suspended prison sentence and two years of probation. “I feel good where I’m at right now,” he told Us in December 2019. “It’s been not easy on anyone. I’m just happy that I’m able to live another day and work and do my thing and be able to do better things for the people around me.” Us broke the news in May 2020 that Chris was seeing Victoria Fuller, who competed on season 24 of The Bachelor. The twosome called it quits, however, at the end of summer 2020. “It’s complicated, but at the same time, I’m just living my life,” Victoria explained on the “Viall Files” in September 2020. “He is an amazing man and he deserves somebody super awesome who’s willing to go to Iowa and live in Iowa and right now, I’m not there yet. Maybe I will be in a couple [of] years.”

Ben Higgins, the 20th Bachelor, got engaged to Lauren Bushnell during the 2016 finale. After The Bachelor, the pair went on to star on their own reality series titled Ben and Lauren: Happily Ever After? on Freeform for one season. In May 2017, the couple announced their split. Ben attempted to find love again during a brief stint on The Bachelor: Winter Games in 2018, but left early. Ben also cohosts a podcast called “Almost Famous” with fellow Bachelor alum Ashley Iaconetti.  In February 2019, Ben revealed he had a girlfriend named Jessica Clarke. Us broke the news in March 2020 that Ben proposed to Jess in Franklin, Tennessee. They wed in November 2021 and revealed in August 2024 they were expecting their first baby. Daughter Winona arrived in February 2025. The next year, the couple shared that they are expecting their second baby. Lauren, for her part, married country singer Chris Lane in October 2019 after a year of dating. They have two sons.

Nick Viall popped the question to Vanessa Grimaldi during season 21 of The Bachelor in 2017. After several months together, the duo called it quits in August 2017. In December 2018, the reality personality, who has had a handful of acting roles in recent months, told Us exclusively that he has “no timeline” for finding a girlfriend. “It’s one of those things — you date, you see what happens,” he explained. “I still hope to meet someone someday. That could be tomorrow, that could be in five years.” After months of speculation, the "Viall Files" podcast host went public with girlfriend Natalie Joy in February 2021. In January 2023, the couple announced that they were engaged after more than two years of dating. They welcomed daughter River Rose in February 2024 and tied the knot the following April. The couple announced in February 2026 that Natalie is pregnant with twins. Nick released a book titled Don't Text Your Ex Happy Birthday: And Other Advice on Love, Sex, and Dating in October 2022.

Following in Jason Mesnick’s footsteps, Arie Luyendyk Jr. proposed to Becca Kufrin during season 22 of The Bachelor, but changed his mind before the season finished airing. The former racecar driver popped the question to runner-up Lauren Burnham during the live After the Final Rose special in March 2018. Months later, Us revealed the couple were expecting their first child. In January 2019, Arie and Lauren told Us exclusively that they were having a baby girl.  Arie and Lauren tied the knot in Hawaii in January 2019. The twosome welcomed their daughter, Alessi, in May 2019. “This was first time she laid eyes on me and I’m forever changed,” Arie gushed on Instagram at the time. “I’m so proud of @laureneburnham. You’re truly incredible and did so good today.” They welcomed their twins, Senna and Lux, in 2021 and daughter Livvy four years later.

Colton Underwood and Cassie Randolph briefly split during the fantasy suites episode of The Bachelor season 23, but the former NFL player sent home both Tayshia Adams and Hannah Godwin to fight for the speech pathologist’s affection. Cassie and Colton confirmed they were together during the finale. In May 2020, the couple announced via Instagram that they split but would remain friends. Two months later, their breakup turned messy after Cassie made an appearance on The Bachelor: The Greatest Seasons — Ever. Colton, for his part, expressed concern that she wasn’t honoring their plan to keep their breakup private, while Cassie accused him of being hypocritical as he planned to write a new chapter of his book about their split. By September 2020, the twosome were on even worse terms when Cassie filed a restraining order against Colton, accusing him of stalking and harassing her via text messages. A judge extended the restraining order to November 6, 2020, after their first hearing, but Cassie later dropped the charges. Colton came out as gay in April 2021 during an interview on Good Morning America. In February 2022, he announced his engagement to Jordan C. Brown, whom he started dating in summer 2021. The pair tied the knot in May 2023 and announced one year later that they were expecting their first baby via surrogate. Their son, Bishop Colton Brown-Underwood, was born in September 2024.

The pilot’s season of the series ended with two breakups. After calling off his engagement to Hannah Ann Sluss while the show was still airing, Peter Weber revealed he still had feelings for Madison Prewett, who left the show during the finale. While Peter and Madison hoped to try to make it work, they confirmed it was over just two days after the March 2020 finale. Less than two weeks later, Peter was spotted out with another one of his contestants: Kelley Flanagan. After weeks of speculation, Us confirmed in April 2020 that the pilot and Kelley were officially in item. Two months later, they confirmed to Chris Harrison that they are planning to move to NYC together. “I remember going in, and I wanted that love story more than anything, and I can honestly say it worked out in the end,” Peter said in June 2020. “Post-show, honestly, I’m doing good. I’m extremely happy. It feels so good to be able to say that and I’m just very hopeful for the future. … I am very, very happy with this one.” Several months later, the pilot revealed in December 2020 that the couple had split. In November 2026, Peter confirmed he had married Jadeyn Carr.

The season 25 Bachelor Matt James ended his relationship with winner Rachael Kirkconnell while the show was airing in 2021 after she made headlines for her past racially insensitive actions, including resurfaced pictures of her at a party on a plantation. “It broke my heart, because this is the last conversation I thought we'd be having. I didn't sign up to have this conversation,” Matt told Rachael about their split during the After the Final Rose special in March 2021. "And I knew that I had to take a step back for you to put in that work that you outlined that you needed to do. And that's something you gotta do on your own. And that's why we can't be in a relationship." While Matt previously ruled out any plans to get back together during his post-show interviews, he confirmed in May 2021 that they were officially on after being spotted together several times the month prior. After four years of dating, Matt confirmed in January 2025 that he and Rachael had called it quits again.

Athlete Clayton Echard technically ended his season alone after breaking up with finalists Gabby Windey and Rachel Recchia — and later being dumped by Susie Evans, who briefly returned after her fantasy suite elimination. However, during the March 2022 finale, the Missouri native revealed that Susie reached out to him post-show. The couple aren't engaged, but they told the host that they were about to settle down in Virginia Beach. After living together for months, Clayton revealed in August 2022 that he was moving to Arizona and Susie was relocating to California. While the pair assured fans that the move wasn’t a sign of a split at the time, they called it quits that September. In September 2023, an unnamed woman claimed she was pregnant with Clayton’s babies following a one-night stand. Clayton repeatedly denied the claims. His paternity trial came to an end in June 2024, with the court siding with Clayton.

Gerry Turner popped the question to Theresa Nist during the Golden Bachelor season 1 final rose ceremony, which aired in November 2023. The pair got married in January 2024, but divorced months later. Later that year, Gerry revealed he was diagnosed with bone marrow cancer weeks before his and Nist’s split. “Unfortunately, there's no cure for it. So that weighs heavily in every decision I make,” he told People in December 2024, admitting that Nist became “less of a priority” as a result. Gerry confirmed he was dating someone new during an April 2025 episode of the “Bachelor Happy Hour” podcast, though he did not share her name. He also noted that he was “optimistic” about his cancer journey after doctors told him he is expected to live past the age of 75.

The second Golden Bachelor lead, Mel Owens, ended his season, which aired in November 2025, in a relationship with Peg Munson. They, however, did not get engaged. "We're on the same page," Peg said during After the Final Rose about whether a proposal was on the horizon. "That’s a love story the way that we get to do it, and to continue to grow our love, continue to spend time with our families and that’s the nice part about being in our 60s in your golden years is being able to do what you want to with that connection you have with someone." Peg announced one year later that the duo had called it quits.

Trista Rehn, who competed for Alex Michel’s heart on season 1 of The Bachelor, starred as the first Bachelorette in 2003. During the finale, she got engaged to Ryan Sutter and the twosome tied the knot on national television in December 2003. They welcomed their first child, a boy named Max, in July 2007. Trista gave birth to their second child, a baby girl named Blakesley, in April 2009. In 2017, the couple, who live in Colorado, revealed Ryan still has the final rose Trista gave him more than a decade ago.

Meredith Phillips accepted a proposal from Ian Mckee during the season 2 finale of The Bachelorette in 2004. A year later, the duo called it quits. Meredith married her high school sweetheart Michael Broady in 2011. Meredith made headlines in 2018 after she alleged an unnamed female masseuse drugged and sexually assaulted her during her time on the ABC series. After her relationship with Andrew Firestone ended, Jen Schefft starred as the third Bachelorette in 2005. While she selected Jerry Ferris during the finale, Jen turned down his proposal and asked him to reconsider popping the question at a later date. During the live After the Final Rose special, however, she revealed the duo had called it quits. Jen went on to marry Joe Waterman in 2009. The pair, who share daughters Mae and Charlotte, reside in Hudson, Ohio. “I grew up outside of Cleveland and my husband is from Cincinnati, so we decided to move home to be closer to family,” Jen, who is a stay-at-home mom, told Us Weekly exclusively.  “People still come up to me and ask about the show quite a bit, which always surprises me!” she continued. “It's been 15 years since I was on the show, and I can't believe people still recognize me. People are always so nice and it's fun to be a small part of pop culture. … I loved my experience on the show and everything it brought into my life, but I'm a much happier person being out of the public eye. I have two daughters who keep me on my toes and a great husband. Life is good!”

After taking three years off, The Bachelorette returned to ABC in 2008 and named DeAnna Pappas the fourth series lead. While she accepted a proposal from Jesse Csincsak during the finale and planned their wedding for May 2009, they called it quits in November 2008. Years later, DeAnna married Stephen Stagliano, whose brother competed on season 5 of The Bachelorette, in Georgia in 2012. The couple share daughter Addison and son Austin. After 11 years of marriage, DeAnna announced her separation from Stephen. “It is with immense sadness, Stephen & I have decided to end our relationship as a couple. We have been working hard for a long time — both as a married couple & as individuals & have come to the conclusion to remain separate,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “We remain loving parents to our beautiful children, Addison & Austin, & will continue to raise them together with love & faith.” In 2025, Us confirmed that DeAnna was arrested after an altercation with Stephen. She was later released on bail and fired back at him in court docs of her own, denying his allegations that she had a drinking problem. DeAnna also filed a restraining order against Stephen.

Jillian Harris and Ed Swiderski got engaged during season 5 of the ABC dating show in 2009. A year later, the twosome announced their breakup in July 2010. Jillian got engaged to her longtime boyfriend, Justin Pasutto, in 2016, and they share two kids: Leo and Annie. “It’s been almost 10 years since I’ve been on the show and so most of the PTSD is gone,” Jillian joked exclusively to Us. “It was such an incredible experience even if it wasn’t ’successful’ i wouldn’t change it for a thing. I learned so much about myself and relationships that still applies to my life today.”  “Its also hard not to connect my current career situation to the Bachelor. I had a great job prior to going on the show, but I do believe that much of life and career today would be much different if I hadn’t taken that chance. I LOVE love working on the website www.jillianharris.com, I love inspiring others, being in a position to give back to charity and also be in a career where i’m able to be super creative,” she continues. “I also was able to stick in the television industry with my role on Love it Or List it, Too, which is also a dream. Yes, I’ve worked hard and loved hard to get to where i am today both professionally and personally, but I often look back and wonder…. what If? Two beautiful children, a handsome dog, a hunky fiancé and a dream job. Is life perfect? HECK no … but I have a ton to be grateful for and i owe a slice of that to the Bachelor family and experience!”

Ali Fedotowsky accepted a proposal from Roberto Martinez during season 6 of The Bachelorette in 2010. After more than a year together, they announced their breakup in November 2011. Ali, now a host and Emerald Duv jewelry designer, married radio personality Kevin Manno in 2017. The couple welcomed daughter Molly in 2016 and son Riley in 2018 and live in Nashville.  “I’d like to think that I would’ve met my husband regardless of the show, but the truth is if I had never gone on The Bachelor and Bachelorette, I’m not sure I would have!” Fedotowsky told Us in 2018. “I met him on another show that I wouldn’t of had the opportunity to host if I hadn’t been on the Bachelorette and now we have a daughter and a son and a beautiful life. I’m even lucky enough that I get to make a living blogging about motherhood, which I’m beyond grateful for. None of this would’ve happened the way it did if I hadn’t gone on that show. I’m beyond grateful for it!”

Ali Fedotowsky accepted a proposal from Roberto Martinez during season 6 of The Bachelorette in 2010. After more than a year together, they announced their breakup in November 2011. Ali, now a host and Emerald Duv jewelry designer, married radio personality Kevin Manno in 2017. The couple welcomed daughter Molly in 2016 and son Riley in 2018 and live in Nashville.

“I’d like to think that I would’ve met my husband regardless of the show, but the truth is if I had never gone on The Bachelor and Bachelorette, I’m not sure I would have!” Fedotowsky told Us in 2018. “I met him on another show that I wouldn’t of had the opportunity to host if I hadn’t been on the Bachelorette and now we have a daughter and a son and a beautiful life. I’m even lucky enough that I get to make a living blogging about motherhood, which I’m beyond grateful for. None of this would’ve happened the way it did if I hadn’t gone on that show. I’m beyond grateful for it!”

Credit: Rodrigo Varela/Getty Images for WE tv

Ashley Hebert and J.P. Rosenbaum got engaged during the season 7 finale of The Bachelorette in 2011. The following year, the twosome tied the knot in December 2012 and their nuptials were documented for a TV special. Ashley gave birth to their first child, a baby boy named Fordham, in September 2014. The pair welcomed their second child, a daughter named Essex, in November 2016. In August 2018, Ashley and J.P. renewed their vows during a trip to Aruba.

Ashley revealed that JP was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome, a rare neurological disorder, is a condition in which the body’s immune system attacks the nerves, in December 2019. “He is in treatment and doing well,” the pediatric dentist said at the time. “It may be a long road to full recovery, but we are so grateful to everyone that has helped us get to a speedy diagnosis and treatment.”

JP, for his part, detailed his symptoms during a December hospital stay: “Things you do every day, like picking up this phone, or buttoning buttons, tying shoelaces, putting on deodorant, just can’t do it. Picking up my kids, can’t do it.” He was discharged on December 9, 2019.

In March 2022, the dentist revealed that she has had a boyfriend for nearly one year.

Credit: Courtesy of Emily Maynard/Instagram

After ending her brief engagement to Brad Womack, Emily Maynard was named the eighth Bachelorette in 2012. She accepted a proposal from Jef Holm during the finale, but the twosome ended their relationship several months after the season finished airing. In June 2014, Emily, who has a daughter named Ricki from her previous relationship, married Tyler Johnson. The couple have since welcomed three sons: Jennings, Gibson and Gatlin. Emily gave birth to the couple’s first daughter, her fifth child, in October 2020.

Desiree Hartsock accepted a proposal from Chris Siegfried during season 9 of The Bachelorette in 2013. Less than two years later, they wed in January 2015. In October 2016, the duo, who reside in Seattle, welcomed their son Asher. Desiree, who works as a wedding dress designer, announced in 2018 that she was pregnant with the pair’s second son. Us broke the news in January 2019 that Desiree gave birth to a second son named Zander. She announced in May 2024 that she was expecting baby No. 3. Son Noah was born in November 2024.

The Georgia-based attorney Andi Dorfman was named the 10th Bachelorette in 2014. Andi accepted a proposal from Josh Murray during the finale. While the pair moved in together in Atlanta, they announced their split in January 2015. Andi documented her Bachelor/Bachelorette journey in her first book, It’s Not Okay, released in 2016. She released her second book, Single State of Mind, in 2018.  “Life after The Bachelorette has been a wild ride for me. People often ask if the show was good or bad for my life and without hesitation, I always say good,” Andi told Us exclusively. “I know had it not been for The Bachelorette I wouldn’t be living life in New York City and being able to say that I am an author working on my third book. And as each season goes on, I may feel a little older but feel proud and grateful to have been part of a show that has so many devoted fans and is still beloved by so many people.”  Andi added that she still speaks to “a lot of people from [her] season,” former host Harrison and a lot of fellow Bachelorettes. “Between the 13 of us, we’ve built a nice, supportive community that I didn’t expect but definitely cherish,” she explained. “Fan encounters are interesting because living in New York the vibe is less fanatic and people are too busy or in too much of a hurry to stop you, but my parents, who live in Georgia, still get people that will recognize their last name or recognize them from being on television, so I think in a funny way they are more of the stars than I am.”  In June 2020, Andi announced via Instagram that she made to move from NYC to Los Angeles. After reconnecting with an old friend named Blaine Hart in Italy during summer 2021, the pair started dating. He proposed on the beach in L.A. in March 2022. The following May, the duo tied the knot in Italy, the same place where they reconnected two years prior.  On August 4, 2024, Andi shared via Instagram that she and Hart were expecting their first child, who arrived in December of that year.

During the season 11 premiere of The Bachelorette, the men met both Kaitlyn Bristowe and fellow season 19 Bachelor contestant Britt Nilsson. The contestants then voted for Kaitlyn to be the lead for the season. During the finale, both Shawn Booth and Nick Viall got down on one knee, but Kaitlyn accepted a ring from Shawn. The pair moved to Nashville and started their lives together offscreen. Fan speculation that the couple called it quits surfaced in summer 2018, but Kaitlyn, who hosts a podcast titled “Off the Vine,” and Shawn, who opened up a gym in Nashville, did not announce the end of their engagement until November 2018. Due to the fact that the pair were together more than two years, Kaitlyn was the first woman from the franchise who got to keep her Neil Lane engagement ring after the breakup even though she did not marry Shawn.  The former Bachelorette confirmed her relationship with fellow Bachelor Nation star Jason Tartick in January 2019. Months later, the duo — who exchanged “I love yous” in April 2019 — moved in together in Nashville and announced they adopted a dog. They adopted a second pup in December 2019. In June 2020, Kaitlyn confirmed that she and Jason picked out an engagement ring before she left to film season 29 of Dancing With the Stars. Almost a year later, the former banker finally popped the question during a May 2021 "Off the Vine" recording session. “It was everything I could have asked for,” Bristowe told Entertainment Tonight. “The words that came out of his mouth were insanely beautiful. We’ve never locked eyes like that in our lives. We were holding hands, so intense, and I was listening to his every word, but still blacked out.” The duo announced their split in August 2023. "Continuing our friendship is incredibly important to both of us," they wrote in a joint social media post at the time. "We feel grateful to be ending our engagement with love and respect for each other. It’s heartbreaking and sad to say goodbye, but our care and admiration for one another will never die."

Credit: Rick Diamond/Getty Images for CMT

JoJo Fletcher accepted a proposal from Jordan Rodgers during the season 12 finale of The Bachelorette in 2012. The twosome moved to Dallas together, but as of January 2019, have no concrete wedding plans. In November 2018, JoJo, who recently launched a clothing line, told Us exclusively that she and Jordan would consider having a televised wedding.  “I would never say no, never, but I think it’s very important that, if it was a televised wedding, that it stays true and organic to us,” she explained. “We would never do a wedding that was just filled with a bunch of Bachelor people that we don’t even know, because that’s not us. But, if we could have it the exact way that we’d want it to be, and allow people to see it as well, then I would say yes.” After Jordan re-proposed in August 2019, the Cash Pad stars told Us that they plan to wed in June 2020. Their nuptials were postponed, however, amid the coronavirus pandemic. Fletcher and Rodgers finally wed in May 2022. Three years later, the couple announced they were expecting their first baby. Daughter Romy Blair arrived in December 2025.

Rachel Lindsay and Bryan Abasolo got engaged during the season 13 finale of The Bachelorette in 2017. “It’s, like, we’re either going to have this 500-plus wedding that we want, or it’s going to be super small,” Rachel said of the duo's nuptials in December 2018. “So I’m going to hurt a lot of feelings, but I’m going to have the wedding that we want, surrounded by the people we love the most and I want to do it as soon as possible. I don’t want to put off a wedding because I’m planning something big for everybody else.” The twosome ultimately tied the knot in August 2019 in Mexico. Rachel, who splits her time between Miami and Los Angeles, works for Extra and hosts the “Higher Learning” podcast with Van Lathan. In January 2022, she released a book titled Miss Me With That: Hot Takes, Helpful Tidbits, and a Few Hard Truths.  Bryan filed for divorce from Rachel in January 2024 after four years of marriage and requested spousal support. Rachel said at the time that she would “eventually” share further details of the split but for the moment was “trying to take it day by day.”

Becca Kufrin accepted a proposal from Garret Yrigoyen during the season 14 finale of The Bachelorette in 2018. The couple told Us exclusively in December 2018 that they have no plans to tie the knot yet. “No dates, no months, no venue,” she said at the time. “The only thing that we’ve talked about that we want are food trucks. I want a great taco truck and a ton of Skee-Ball machines so everyone can just play games.” In August 2019, the pair moved to San Diego together and adopted a Corgi puppy named Miss Minno.  The twosome made headlines in June 2020 after Becca and Rachel recorded an emotional podcast about the Black Lives Matter movement, in which they discussed Garrett’s public support for police. “For those who are curious about my relationship with Garrett at this point, all I can say right now is I don’t know,” Becca said in June 2020." I can’t give anything more than that. It’s something that we are trying to work through and discuss and do work on at home at this time and that’s where the work will remain and that’s really the best can give you at this point.” Three months later, Becca confirmed that the pair went their separate ways. “After many conversations, we came to this decision. It wasn’t something that we just arrived at one night,” Becca explained on the “Bachelor Happy Hour” podcast. “It wasn’t based solely off of one Instagram post or somebody else’s opinions or comments. There’s much more to it. To any relationship, there’s a lot of layers, and it’s not for me to divulge details. It’s no one’s business other than what I’m telling you right now.” Becca returned to ABC for season 7 of Bachelor in Paradise and met boyfriend Thomas Jacobs. Becca proposed to Jacobs in May 2022 after less than a year of dating. Five months later, Thomas popped the question to Becca during a beach trip to Ojai, California.  The duo announced in April 2023 that they were expecting their first child. Their baby boy was born in September 2023. One month later, the twosome said “I do” at a San Diego courthouse. Kufrin revealed in October 2025 that she and Jacobs were expecting their second baby. Their second son, Steven, was born in April 2026.

Former pageant queen Hannah Brown, who was the 15th Bachelorette, broke off her engagement to winner Jed Wyatt during the July 2019 finale after learning he had a girlfriend at home. While she briefly rekindled her relationship with runner-up Tyler Cameron, who was spotted leaving her Los Angeles home in August 2019, Hannah shifted her focus to winning Dancing With the Stars in September 2019 when she was named a contestant on season 28. Hannah and partner Alan Bersten took home the mirrorball trophy during the November 2019 finale. Hannah went public with model boyfriend Adam Woolard in February 2021. She published a memoir titled God Bless This Mess: Learning to Live and Love Through Life's Best (and Worst) Moments in November 2021. In August 2023, she announced her engagement to Woolard after more than two years of dating. They wed in July 2025.

Hairstylist Clare Crawley's unprecedented season 16 journey came to an early end after she fell in love with Dale Moss when there was still 16 men remaining. During a November 2020 episode, Harrison gave Clare and Dale one-on-one time and she ultimately broke things off with the other suitors and accepted a proposal from Dale (and Tayshia Adams took over where Clare left off.) In November 2020, the pair announced via Instagram Live that they recently celebrated three months together and were house hunting in Sacramento, California. Their happiness was short-lived, however. Clare and Dale ended their engagement in January 2021. “We appreciate the love and support we’ve received from so many people, but this is the healthiest decision for both of us at this time,” Dale wrote via Instagram at the time. A month later, Us exclusively revealed that the twosome are back together after they were spotted holding hands in Florida. Less than one year after giving things another shot, Us confirmed in September 2021 that Clare and Dale split again. One year later, Us revealed Clare was dating a man named Ryan Dawkins. He proposed in Las Vegas in October 2022. Clare and Ryan wed in February 2023. Clare announced via Instagram in July 2023 that she and Ryan are expecting their first baby via surrogate. “Our laundry is about to get a whole lot cuter in 2024!!” she captioned a video of the couple putting a onesie on a clothesline that read, “Worth the wait.” Clare confirmed her daughter’s arrival in January 2024. “She’s here!” she wrote via Instagram, sharing a photo that showed her hugging Ryan in a hospital room.
