#3561. This GTA 6-Inspired Keycap Set Will Make The Wait For A PC Version Slightly Easier

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now just a couple of hours away in some parts of the world. That is, if you're planning to play on either Xbox or PlayStation. The wait for a PC version is still ongoing, with Rockstar yet to indicate when it plans to release that port. In the meantime, however, you can start ensuring that your setup is at least ready for when it arrives.

High-end keycap manufacturer GMK has revealed a new set that is clearly inspired by GTA 6 and Vice City, without explicitly mentioning either. The new set, named Neon Vice, features black keycaps with an array of colored alphas and numerical keys, all drawing from the pink, orange, and purple colors of Rockstar's impending sequel. Novelty keycaps include images of speedboats across choppy water, palm trees, and alligators, and the Vice City skyline.

Like most GMK sets, the keycaps are constructed from double-shot ABS plastic, which should ensure fantastic legibility with use over time. What isn't normal is the price, however. GMK keycap sets are priced at a premium, and Neon Vice is no exception. Expect to pay $170 for the base kit, and an additional $45 if you want the novelty keys on top of that. Preorders open for the kit today across multiple vendors around the world.

That's a lot more than the game itself, so if you haven't been bitten by the custom keyboard bug, it's probably best to just continue waiting. Thankfully the gap between console and PC versions for GTA 6 might not be as large as previous Rockstar titles, with a report suggesting that it might arrive in early 2027. If you are playing on console you can pre-load the game right now ahead of its launch, which will start for lucky players in New Zealand very soon.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Johnny Depp returning to theaters in Ebenezer on the 2026 movie schedule, renewed interest has grown in whether he'll ever play Captain Jack Sparrow again. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has already confirmed that discussions have taken place about bringing Depp back for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, although nothing has been officially announced. Now another familiar face from the original movies has weighed in, and I have to admit, this is one reunion I'd love to see happen.

Mackenzie Crook, who played the perpetually confused Ragetti in the first three Pirates movies, recently discussed the possibility of returning to the franchise during an appearance on The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast. The actor, who starred alongside Lee Arenberg's Pintel as one of the series' most entertaining comedic duos, hasn't appeared in a Pirates movie since 2007's At World's End. Although nearly 20 years later, he sounds more than willing to dig out that wooden eye. Crook explained:

Yes, I think I would for the hell of it. It would be so interesting – obviously it would depend on the script – to even just have a cameo to see what happened to those characters, Pintel and Ragetti, what happened to them after we last saw them. Again, I was really fond of those characters and working with Lee Arenberg, who plays Pintel. Yeah, we had a blast doing that stuff. It was great.

I would absolutely love this. Pintel and Ragetti were two of my favorite supporting characters from the original trilogy, and their ridiculous behavior provided some great comic relief between all the sword fights and increasingly more extravagant set pieces.

For anybody who needs a refresher, the pair started as members of Barbossa's cursed crew in The Curse of the Black Pearl. Ragetti was the skinny, somewhat dimwitted pirate with a wooden eye. Pintel was his considerably louder and equally incompetent partner.

Somehow, they survived three movies filled with undead pirates, sea monsters and increasingly complicated betrayals. That's honestly impressive considering how frequently they seemed to have no idea what was going on. While I certainly want to see Johnny Depp return as Jack Sparrow, I think bringing back characters like these could be just as important to making another Pirates movie feel connected to the originals.

Crook also had some interesting memories of working on the films. During the interview, he recalled the sometimes exhausting experience of shooting aboard actual ships at sea. He also discussed the rather uncomfortable process of bringing Ragetti's wooden eye to life, which required wearing two contact lenses, including one designed to create the appearance of wood grain.

Apparently, playing a pirate wasn't quite as glamorous as it looked. The actor also reflected on the amount of practical filmmaking involved in the original trilogy. Although the movies relied heavily on visual effects, Crook remembered productions where crews actually rigged ships with explosives rather than recreating everything digitally. He described those experiences as some of the last examples of old-fashioned blockbuster filmmaking.

I think that's part of what makes those first three movies so much fun to revisit with a Disney+ subscription. Even when the stories got complicated, something fantastically chaotic about watching these characters run around enormous pirate ships, usually making whatever situation they were in considerably worse. Of course, whether any of them actually return is another matter.

Bruckheimer previously confirmed that he's been speaking with Depp about a sixth movie, although the project remains in development. Depp recently suggested he'd be interested in helping give the franchise a proper sendoff, particularly if it meant working with Bruckheimer again.

Meanwhile, other original cast members have expressed interest in returning. Orlando Bloom has discussed the possibility of another Pirates movie, though there's still no indication that Will Turner will be part of whatever Disney ultimately decides to make.

That's really where we stand. There's no confirmed cast or release date for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, and Crook's comments are just an expression of interest, not evidence he's been approached.

I do like his idea of a cameo that lets audiences catch up with Pintel and Ragetti. It's been almost two decades since we last saw the two idiots, and I can't help wondering what they've been doing with themselves.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3559. Zara Tindall Shows Cheltenham Why She's The Queen of Race Day Dressing

Zara Tindall didn’t let the cold snap stop her from enjoying a day at the races on Friday. Accompanied by her close friend Dolly Maude and country-set favorite fashion designer Jade Holland Cooper, the daughter of Princess Anne and granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II brought a dash of regal glamour to the proceedings following a glitzy night out in support of Prince William.

And while the sun may have been out, the Olympic equestrian still needed to wrap up against the chill. Tindall opted for a long plaid coat from L'Agence, a Purdey roll-neck jumper in brown, and a fascinator from Sally-Ann Provan. She accessorized with a new pair of Hector Lion earrings, a new Fairfax & Favor handbag, and completed the look with leather boots, also from Fairfax & Favor.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

Dolly, on the other hand, wore an avant-garde feather coat with knee-high boots and what looked to be a pair of emerald tights.

The pair were last spotted together in October, when they attended the William Hill Showcase Meeting at Cheltenham, but their friendship goes way back. Long considered Zara’s best friend, Dolly became Princess Anne’s lady-in-waiting in 2024. A former NHS midwife, she helped to deliver Zara’s third child, Lucas Tindall, on the floor of Zara’s bathroom at Gatcombe Park after the plan for the birth went awry in 2021.

Jade Holland Cooper and Zara Tindall on day one of The November Meeting at Cheltenham racecourse

But Dolly’s bond with the niece of King Charles III goes back long before that. (Not for nothing did Zara’s husband, Mike Tindall, joke that the 53-year-old is “more important than I am.”) Dolly was Zara’s maid of honor when the pair tied the knot, and when Zara split from her then-fiancé, jockey Richard Johnson, in 2003, the pair moved in together—they still live close by in the Cotswolds.

Having worked as a maternity practitioner in the NHS in Gloucestershire for 13 years, Dolly also did some philanthropic work using her maternity expertise, working in the unit of a hospital in Kambia, Sierra Leone for a month in 2013. At Kambia, she taught staff basic nursing skills. Before qualifying as a nurse, Dolly studied fashion and Cordon Bleu cookery at Eastbourne College of Food and Fashion, graduating in 1989.

Zara Tindall also braved the stormy weather for a day at Cheltenham with Dolly in October

Dolly Maude is known for her love of horses—a passion she shares with Zara and Princess Anne—and is often seen in Ascot’s royal box alongside the Princess Royal. In March 2024, she made her first official appearance as the Princess Royal’s lady-in-waiting, a momentous occasion that marked a new phase of her enduring bond with the royal family.

The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

Concerning Dolly’s appointment, another friend of Mrs. Maude's told The Telegraph, “She’s such a great girl. For the Princess Royal, it’s a perfect fit because of their shared love of dogs and horses. She’s not only extremely close to Zara, she also gets on brilliantly with the Princess. She’s fiercely loyal and discreet. It’s a great match.”

While much of Zara Tindall’s time this season has been spent touring the country’s most prestigious racing meets, she still found time to support her cousin, Prince William, at one of his treasured annual traditions. The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

Zara showcased her characteristically elegant style, donning a sapphire-blue Rebecca Vallance short-sleeved midi number, aptly named the “Crown Jewel” dress, which she paired with Kiki McDonough earrings. It is not the first time that the royal has lent her support to Prince William’s second-longest patronage: she also joined the crowd at the Tusk Awards in 2025, donning Rebecca Vallance again, and tearing up at the Prince of Wales’ speech in honor of those who gave their lives as rangers.

Zara Tindall and the Marchioness of Bath at the Tusk Awards

#3558. These Are Some Of The Biggest Snubs At The Game Awards 2026

The nominees for The Game Awards have been announced. Some of the biggest games--and those that aren't out yet--make appearances on the list, including Grand Theft Auto 6 and Phantom Blade Zero, but some of the games could've--and maybe should've--been nominated in multiple categories. So, let's go over some of the biggest snubs at this year's TGAs.

Let's start with the big one: Game of the Year. You've got six games nominated here: 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto 6, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. All of them are fabulous and well-deserved, but a couple of games are missing: House House's co-op adventure Big Walk and Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker. They appear elsewhere, sure, but I think they deserve GOTY contention, as well.

Let's move onto Best Performance. You've got some stellar voice work here: Angela Sant’Albano as Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem, Liam McIntyre as James "Logan" Howlett in Marvel's Wolverine, Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos in GTA 6, Patrick Gibson as James Bond in 007 First Light, and Rahul Kohli as Arjun Devraj in Saros. Not taking anything away from these incredible voice talents, but Nick Apostolides as Leon Kennedy in Resident Evil Requiem, Sean Durrie as Dylan Faden in Control Resonant, and Will de Renzy-Martin as Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker deserve some recognition, too.

Marathon could've easily been nominated for Best Art Direction and Best Action Game. Overwatch and WoW/WoW: Forever would've made sense in the Best Ongoing Game category. Denshattack's soundtrack is too good not to be nominated for Best Score and Music. And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse could slot into a number of categories, including Best Action/Adventure Game, Best Art Direction, and Best Narrative.

There are probably many others that have come out this year that maybe could--and maybe should--have been nominated but weren't for one reason or another. (Note: GameSpot is among the publications that contribute to the nomination process.)

Regardless, we won't have to wait too long to learn what games win what categories, as The Game Awards will air live on December 10 at 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET.

#3556. 007 First Light Might Be The End Of The Line For James Bond’s Favorite Watch

After months of searching and numerous potential frontrunners, Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond. It's lead to some questions about whether he's too famous or too old for the role, whether or not he looks like Bond, and just how different his portrayal might be to those that came before him. For some others, however, the questions is far more direct: What watch is he going to wear?

James Bond has long had recognizable brand associations, but one that has endured has been the partnership with luxury watch maker Omega. Bond was first seen wearing an Omega in 1995's GoldenEye, and was mostly recently seen sporting the latest iteration of the Seamaster Diver 300m in this year's 007 First Light. Although not a new film in the series, First Light still featured its own unique take on the Seamaster, the first ever created for a videogame, with Omega adding it to its bursting 007 collection that it makes available for purchase.

So given that it's been three decades, why could First Light be the last iteration of James Bond wearing an Omega? Simply put, Robert Pattinson doesn't wear one, and has very recently become a brand ambassador for one of Omega's Swiss competitors, Jaeger-LeCoultre. There's no confirmation that Pattinson's obligations will directly influence a brand deal between Omega and new Bond owners Amazon, but the omission of any watch at all in the announcement trailer sure has cause some speculation.

Daniel Craig, during his tenure as Bond, was Omega's chief ambassador, often wearing unreleased models to drum up interest for imminent releases. That might not be the case with Pattinson, which could suggest a change for what timepiece his Bond decides to switch to.

If Bond were to jump from Omega to JLC, it would be somewhat fitting. The watch maker manufactures some extremely elegant pieces with a rich history associated with each line. But none makes as much sense as the rectangular Reverso. The watch is distinct in its design, allowing the wearer to rotate the face and flip it 180 degrees, with a variety of designs on the back. Initially created for polo players to protect their prized wristwatches, you can clearly see a lot of potential for some weird and creative Bond gadgetry to intersect with a design like this.

Or maybe Pattinson will arrive on the block with yet another Seamaster Diver 300m, and all of this would've been wishful thinking. But if he doesn't, and this truly is the last we'll see of Bond with Omega, at least First Light introduced one of the better entries in the entire collection.

We’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious. This has not been the best season of The Traitors. In fact, you could easily say this has been a below-average season. Fans on social media and those I have talked to in real life seem to all be in agreement on that. There’s a growing consensus that the show needs to change. I think producers are going to listen, though I’m terrified they’re going to misunderstand the why.

The biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities. The US version of The Traitors has historically relied on reality television personalities to provide the drama and bring their fanbases. This season, NBC decided to move the property from Peacock to network television and cast it like a more traditional competition show with randoms. It would be easy to just look at that decision and blame all the problems on the newbies, but that’s actually not the right takeaway.

The biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes. The show simply does not work in an hour-long time slot on NBC. In theory, the episodes on Peacock are the same length, as they’re typically between an hour and an hour and ten minutes. Because they’re on streaming, however, that runtime is the actual length of each episode. On network television, an hour-long time slot is actually forty-two minutes or so of real content, which isn’t even close to the amount of time the players need to complete one cycle of the game.

That means every single episode, the editors are making an impossible choice. They can either not include one or more major elements of the show (the breakfast, the mission, the roundtable and the turret), they can completely remove all of the strategy scenes that happen between those major elements, or they can drop most of the confessionals where the players talk directly to the camera and tell us their motivations and theories. There is simply no way to get through all of that in forty-two minutes. So, that has left every episode feeling either incomplete because it didn’t make it through a full cycle of the game, or feeling like a highlight video that simply recaps the basics of what happened.

That format and structure are the problem. The runtime is the problem. It’s not the cast. Even with less confessionals and less screentime, we’ve gotten good content from these players. I’m not saying the Traitors: New Blood cast is better than the cast on Big Brother 14 or Survivor: Heroes vs Villains, but there are some breakout personalities here and plenty of likeable, solid characters who have popped and would have looked even better with more of a chance to talk to the camera.

Victor is an all-time great Traitors character and should be a reality television mainstay moving forward. He’s electric. I’m personally obsessed with Jay and have had probably ten conversations with people trying to figure out his vibe and what’s going on in his head. It’s not just those two standouts either. There are a half dozen or so other players who play hard and are capable of delivering strong confessionals. Joe, Katie, Tomica, Michael and Shane have all had great moments, and when given a chance, secondary characters like Wyatt, Clyde, Abby, Abbey, Kriste, Ben, Morgan and others have delivered too. They’re just not always getting the screentime because, once again, every episode feels like it’s set on 1.5X speed.

Survivor and The Amazing Race have lengthened their episodes in recent years to help develop the characters and let the episodes breathe more. That’s the obvious solution here for The Traitors. It either needs to move to 90 minutes, or it needs to move back to Peacock. What it absolutely does not need to do is give up on casting newbies. The UK and other countries have had fantastic seasons using randoms, and in an ideal world, it would be a delight to watch Peacock/ NBC switch back and forth between a season with reality stars and a season with plumbers, farmers and firefighters.

I love The Traitors. It’s one of my favorite shows on television, and despite the obvious format issues, I still enjoyed the content we got this season. I’d like to see producers listen to the fan frustration and make a change, but those alterations should be exclusively focused on the format and not on casting.

#3553. Civilization Dev Lays Off 1/3 Of Staff, New XCOM Game Facing “Development Struggles” – Report

The video game industry's woes continue as Take-Two's 2K division has confirmed that one third of the staff at Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games is being laid off.

Bloomberg confirmed the cuts, which will impact around 60 people. As part of the downsizing, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is leaving.

A spokesperson for Firaxis confirmed the restructuring to Bloomberg, saying the cuts are part of an effort to "focus on design, technology, and player experience."

"These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis," the spokesperson said.

According to Bloomberg's sources, Firaxis is working on a new XCOM game, but it has faced "development struggles" and missed a major milestone this past summer. The game is still going ahead, though the sources said it "may face a shakeup" due to the layoffs.

The latest game from Firaxis, Sid Meier's Civilization VII, was released in February 2025 and had numerous technical issues upon release, though the experience has been improved since then with updates. The entire Civilization series has sold more than 80 million units.

As for the XCOM series, the latest entry from Firaxis was 2020's XCOM: Chimera Squad, and before that was 2016's XCOM 2.

Firaxis was co-founded by Sid Meier in 1996, so 2026 is the studio's 30th anniversary. Take-Two bought the company in 2005 and put the studio and the franchise under the 2K banner.

#3552. As Hollywood Battles AI, Pedro Pascal Says Making Behemoth! Filled Him with “a Tremendous Amount of Hope”

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

“The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

Gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”

“Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” said Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”

“Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3551. 10 Hacks Every Waze User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Waze is a crowdsourced navigation app designed to help you get where you're going as quickly and with as much information about your route as possible. Where Google Maps and Apple Maps offer relatively straightforward directions, Waze tries to outsmart these alternatives by integrating real-time community feedback about hazards, speed traps, road closures, and more. If you are switching to Waze or using it alongside your other navigation tools, these are the hacks to help you maximize everything the app has to offer.

If you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, Waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule. You can set up "Time to leave" reminders in advance for individual planned drives, or you can sync your calendar to receive notifications for scheduled events. Calendar sync connects to your device's default calendar app, but you can change this to a third-party alternative if you prefer. Calendar events must include a navigable address to trigger reminders, and you must select Plan a drive in Waze for the event.

Waze has a feature called "child reminders," which are notifications to check for children before you get out of the car. This is clearly an incredibly important use case, but you can also use these alerts for custom messages, like "Don't forget the groceries!" In Waze, tap the menu button > Settings > Reminders > Child reminder and select Custom message.

Variable speed limits, especially on unfamiliar routes, can result in you speeding when you don't mean to. But Waze can alert you if you exceed a customized speed threshold so you aren't caught by surprise or at higher risk of being ticketed. From the menu, go to Settings > Speedometer and turn on Show speedometer. Tap Speeding threshold to select what limit you want to trigger alerts, and turn on Alert at threshold if you want Waze to play a sound.

Waze offers a wealth of information on routes to help drivers navigate obstacles and hazards, but this can clutter your map and distract you from the most critical information, especially in congested, high-traffic areas. Waze says it limits and prioritizes alerts automatically, but you can actually customize which alerts you see based on what's most important to you. From the menu, go to Settings > Alerts and reports > Reports and select the relevant alerts.

In the same Alerts and reports menu, you can enable Alert while driving, which will give you an audio warning and an onscreen pop-up about your selected hazards. This allows you to run navigation via a different map app (like Google Maps or Apple Maps) in the foreground while still getting Waze data in the background.

Waze integrates with toll road and HOV lane passes, so if you have an express or fast lane subscription, your route will optimize for it. If you don't, Waze can still account for HOV lane eligibility if you tell it how many passengers are in your car. From the menu, go to Settings > Toll and HOV passes and tap the plus icon to add your pass(es) from the list. If you need to add your passenger count instead, you can do so from View routes and enable the HOV option.

If you're driving through an unfamiliar, highly congested, or poorly designed area, you can ask Waze to help you avoid tricky maneuvers, such as crossing multiple lanes of traffic or turning left at intersections without lights. This prioritizes ease over speed using protected green arrows, roundabouts, and right turns. From the menu, go to Settings > Navigation, Avoid difficult intersections and select Always. You can also ask Waze to avoid toll roads, ferries, freeways, and unpaved roads.

Waze has a built-in audio player that syncs with your preferred listening platform—such as Spotify, YouTube Music, and Pandora—so you can control your music without having to navigate between apps. (As Waze is a Google product, Apple Music isn't included.) Simply tap the music icon on the map to select your audio player and hit Accept. If you don't see the icon, go to Settings > Audio player and turn on Show on the map.

If you want to make audio directions more interesting, you can select a celebrity or character voice to help you navigate. Recent appearances include Bill Hader's Cat in the Hat and Ziggy Marley. Tap the speaker icon > Current voice to search for the voice or language you want to use. You can also record directions in your own voice.

#3550. How GTA 6 Is Eligible For The Game Awards This Year

We've known for some time that Grand Theft Auto 6 was likely to be eligible for The Game Awards, and now that 2026's TGA nominees are live, it's official: Not only is GTA eligible, but it actually has the most nominations of any game.

That's somewhat of an unusual situation, given that GTA 6 reviews are not yet live. Regardless, this invites some questions of how or why GTA 6 can be eligible before reviews go out and before the game is available. (Nominations even confirmed a key actor in the game.)

For months, the official website for The Game Awards has listed November 20, 2026 at 9 PM PT as the cutoff date for this year's ceremony, which means that any game that launches before that time can be considered for nomination. As GTA VI is scheduled to launch one day earlier, on November 19, GTA 6 is eligible just like any other game already released this year.

Now, before torches are lit and pitchforks are sharpened, evidence suggests that date was not put in place specifically for GTA to be eligible this year: The Friday before Thanksgiving has routinely been the cutoff for TGA nominations.

Last year, the cutoff was November 21, as referenced in this Polygon article regarding Dispatch's eligibility. In 2024, eligibility was cut off on November 22, as evidenced in this Polygon article exploring the games that missed 2024 and were eligible in 2025.

2018 was the last time a Rockstar project was eligible for most categories at The Game Awards, as Red Dead Redemption II landed 10 nominations and four wins. Notably, one of those wins was not Game of the year, which went to Sony Santa Monica for the God of War reboot.

Grand Theft Auto VI's eligibility for TGA 2026 was never in doubt--well, unless it got delayed again. Now that we're clear of that scenario, it's only a matter of time until we see just how many trophies are headed to Vice City.

#3549. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

In unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just announced that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form."

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal

Hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

#3548. This Fighting Game Is Nominated For A TGA Despite Development Shutting Down

Earlier today, Geoff Keighley announced all of the nominees for The Game Awards 2026, the annual celebration of gaming held in Los Angeles. Among expected nominees Grand Theft Auto VI, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Control Resonant was one surprising name: 2XKO has been nominated for Best Fighting Game, despite Riot Games announcing the end of the game's lifecycle earlier this year.

Riot announced that "active development" for the fighting game, featuring characters from League of Legends, would end in December 2026. "Over the last few months, we’ve been monitoring 2XKO’s trajectory closely, and what we’ve seen is painting a clear, consistent picture," Riot said at the time. "While a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there’s an incredible community that plays every day, we haven’t seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability,”

Riot's fighter is joined in the Best Fighting Game category by Invincible Vs., Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Avatar Legends, and My Hero Academia: All's Justice. 2XKO is also not the only game on this list whose future is in jeopardy; soon after it launched in April, Invincible Vs. developer Quarter up laid off reportedly 75% of its staff, while saying that future updates were dependent on the game's overall sales.

Grand Theft Auto VI received the most nominations for a single game at this year's ceremony with eight, including Game of the Year. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem tied for the second-most nominations with six each, while Phantom Blade Zero rounded out the top three with five nominations. Nintendo earned the most nominations for a single publisher, meanwhile, with 12 across the event's 30 awards.

The Game Awards is set to take place December 10 live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California.

#3547. Patriots QB Drake Maye's Wife Ann Michael Breaks Silence After Ankle Injury

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will “always” have a fan in wife Ann Michael Maye, even if he’s sidelined from an injury.

Ann Michael, 23, has broken her silence after Drake, 24, suffered an ankle injury during the team’s Sunday, November 15, game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

“ILY always,” she wrote via her Instagram Story on Tuesday, November 17, alongside a red heart emoji.

Ann Michael, who has been married to the NFL player since June 2025, also shared a photo of the couple kissing before Drake took the field in Europe.

Ann Michael wore a camel coat, over a navy top as she leaned in and smooched her husband. She wore a red clip in her hair as well, giving a subtle nod to the Patriots’ red, white and blue color palate.

Drake was dressed in the team’s white uniforms, holding his silver helmet in his hand as he paused for the pregame good luck kiss.

Ann Michael’s sweet message comes two days after Drake was sidelined in Sunday’s game during the first quarter after Lions’ defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked him.

Hutchinson, 26, was also hurt after celebrating the play, exiting the game shortly after Drake with a knee injury. (NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hutchinson’s initial tests revealed a torn ACL in his right knee, but the Lions haven’t released an official report.)

ESPN reported on Monday, November 16, that Drake will miss “an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season” with a suspected fractured ankle. The team hasn’t confirmed his exact injury.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained on Monday’s WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show that Drake “stayed back” in Germany “out of caution” before making plans to return to the U.S. for further evaluation.

“He’ll be traveling back here shortly, but [we] just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely,” Vrabel, 51, said.

Drake, meanwhile, has yet to address his injury, but his wife has already indicated that she’ll be by his side through thick or thin.

The couple, who are childhood sweethearts, have already handled a whirlwind first year of marriage — and they aren’t showing any signs of stopping. After tying the knot in summer 2025, Drake led the Patriots to his first Super Bowl appearance in February 2026.

While the team lost to the Seattle Seahawks, Drake and Ann Michael have bonded over their new life together in Boston, far from what they both grew up knowing.

“Moving to somewhere so completely different, being away from all of our friends and family is probably the most challenging part,” Ann Michael exclusively told Us in August. “Luckily, we have great teammates and great friends here that have really made the New England area feel like home, which is great.”

She noted, “But you know, we’re both from North Carolina. Our parents live in the same neighborhood, and then we went to college in North Carolina, so we were never too far from family. That’s been the biggest adjustment.”

Amazon is offering early Black Friday discounts on like-new versions of its 2024 Kindles, with prices starting at $152.99 for the Paperwhite and savings of $27 to $75 across five models that include the color-screen Colorsoft and the pen-equipped Kindle Scribe. All five are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The company introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon has tested and certified to look and work like new.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite (16GB) is down to $152.99 from $179.99 and covers just about everything most people need for everyday reading, including enough storage for thousands of ebooks. Its seven-inch, 300ppi glare-free display is larger than the previous generation’s 6.8-inch screen, with faster page turns, an adjustable warm light, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life. As PCMag notes in its review, it's a great option for readers who don't need color or handwriting features.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $190.99 from $224.99, making it just $38 more than the like-new Paperwhite (16GB). For that relatively small difference, you're doubling the storage to 32GB and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft (16GB) is down to $220.99 from $260.99 and offers something the Paperwhite models can’t: a color E-Ink display, which makes it well suited to comics, graphic novels, illustrated books, and travel guides. Its seven-inch screen shows that color content at 150ppi while keeping text at a sharp 300ppi, and you can mark passages in multiple highlight colors to keep your notes organized. That said, colors are noticeably more muted than on a conventional tablet, and battery life tops out at eight weeks, compared with 12 weeks on the Paperwhite.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $243.99 from $287.99, making it just $23 more than the standard like-new Colorsoft. For that modest increase, you're getting twice the storage at 32GB, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $284.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

With FBI now in its ninth season on the 2026 TV schedule, the stakes have certainly been rising, and I’m not just talking about the professional ones. A show like FBI not only digs into the work aspect of the characters but the personal lives as well, even if it’s not shown as much. This week’s episode had a particularly surprising personal update for one of the characters, and that made me realize I had to ask the stars about spinoff potential.

Shantel VanSanten returned to FBI as Special Agent Nina Chase in Monday’s episode, “Posterity,” which marked her second appearance on the series since FBI: Most Wanted’s cancellation in 2025. Her return came just a couple of weeks after it was revealed that Nina had been offered a job to lead her own task force in San Diego, leading Scola (John Boyd) to question the logistics of their relationship and raising their son, Dougie. As Nina continued to pack and get in one last case at 26 Fed, Scola was still wrestling with how they were going to make things work. Ultimately, he told Nina he was going to put in a transfer and follow her to San Diego, meaning another FBI exit could be looming.

As Scola pointed out, though, it will still probably be a while until the transfer goes through. However, with him eventually moving out to California and Scolina taking the FBI by storm down there, this has spinoff potential written all over it. It would be fun to follow Scola and Nina in San Diego as Nina led her own task force, but would it ever happen? VanSanten and Boyd gave their take to CinemaBlend and, hilariously, have their own opinions on the ordeal:

FBI has been growing as a franchise, like any Dick Wolf series, so it’s totally logical to wonder about a spinoff coming from this update. Having two fan-favorite characters moving across the country for the job would certainly be a missed opportunity for another series, in my humble opinion. While it sounds like there aren’t any plans, and Boyd seems to be sticking around on FBI for the time being, if VanSanten has her way, we very well could be getting a Scolina spinoff at some point in the future. While we wait and hope for that, I'm just glad that it seems like Nina is finally getting closure.

As for what could happen in a potential Scolina spinoff, well, the possibilities are endless. Nina leading her own task force and seeing how she evolves in that leadership position would definitely be a great focus point. Scola would probably be settling into a new FBI field office, but the two of them would still stick to their deal of not going on cases together. We’d also probably get more of them and Dougie, who we definitely have not seen enough of. The story is there, and so are the characters, and I would love it if it happened. But if not, I’d hope that Boyd isn’t leaving FBI any time soon.

Now, for the time being, Scola will continue working out of 26 Fed. Considering all the cast changes that FBI has been through in recent years, I’m hoping that Boyd doesn’t leave the series any time soon, no matter how much I want a Scolina spinoff. Nina may be moving, but fans can still see Scola and co. in new episodes of FBI on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#3544. BioWare Is Dead, But Mass Effect’s Spiritual Successor Exodus Just Gave Us A Glimpse of A Spicy Romance

For the first time since its announcement during December 2023's The Game Awards, players are getting a look at the female player-character from its upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus--which was full of Mass Effect DNA back when we previewed it in September.

The default female version of main character Jun Aslan was revealed today via a seven-minute featurette showing off both female-Jun's face and a bit more of the game itself. The trailer also provided a glimpse of a brief romance scene between female-Jun and Suliman, who is one of the game's romanceable NPCs.

When GameSpot previewed the game, only male-Jun was playable, and we didn't get a chance to romance Suliman, but we did manage to earn his approval, suggesting he may be into both masculine and feminine Jun. We also didn't see the character creator, but there certainly appears to be one, as we see Jun sporting a different look during the romantic encounter with Suliman, with voice actress Carina Corti (Mafia: The Old Country, Little Death) providing Jun's voice throughout both scenes.

Jun's male character model recently got a complete makeover after players complained his original look wasn't pleasing to the eye, but up until today, it wasn't clear who was voicing him. Today, Archetype shared that Stephen Oyoung (Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Spider-Man 2) will be voicing the character.

The female-Jun reveal is followed by a featurette called Scrappy Salvager, featuring a behind-the-scenes look at Jun's origins and the way players' decision can impact Jun's trajectory early on in the game.

"We think of players as the co-authors of our story, and that applies to Jun as well," game director Chris King explains in the video. 

Art director Mark Anderson describes Jun as a "little fish in a really big pond," rather than starting off as a typical hero ready to save the world. Additionally, the featurette goes into more detail about Jun's "precognition" ability, which allows them to see glimpses of possible futures. If interpreted correctly, these premonitions may help players make choices that benefit them. But misunderstanding them may lead to consequences that expand far beyond Jun and their friends. Due to the way the game's time dilation mechanic works, player choices can have unexpected effects that impact civilizations for centuries.

After the death of BioWare, it seems the Mass Effect formula will live on in Exodus, with its vast worlds, strange alien races, NPC romances, and narrative choices. It shouldn't come as a surprise, of course--Exodus developer Archetype Entertainment was founded in 2019 by BioWare veterans James Ohlen, Drew Karpshyn, and Chad Robertson.

Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

#3543. Sam Altman Is “Still Unknowable” to Andrew Garfield, Even After Playing the OpenAI Co-Founder in Artificial

In Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this new generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield said about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's important to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”

Barbaro said the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the company, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

For Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more."

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci said. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the issue that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with new distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he said about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”

“They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a big thing.”

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3542. Ring's New $250 Indoor Camera Drone Sounds Terrifying

Ring made its name with its smart doorbells with built-in cameras, and now sells more indoor cameras than any other company, capturing more than 40% of the market. When you've already moved tens of millions of devices (enough to raise serious concerns about their use as part of the surveillance state), you always need to keep innovating, and today, the company announced a product it has been working on for a decade: an indoor camera drone powered by artificial intelligence. I got a chance to check it out during a media event yesterday, and I can report that, as harbingers of our dystopian future go, it is only mildly terrifying.

The drone camera is one of two products in the company's new Ring Robotics line, alongside a "rover cam" that looks kind of like the canister of a vacuum cleaner attached to an iPad. While the Ring Rover Cam is priced at $999.99 and targeted at businesses, the Ring Drone Cam is a much more affordable $249.99, reasonable enough that it will appeal to consumers looking for another way to keep (robot) eyes on their stuff.

The drone camera records 2K video and has a 148-degree field of view and the ability to rotate 360 degrees. It works with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms, as well as the Alexa Home Map. It has a flight time of eight minutes, and once it returns to its base station, it takes around an hour to fully recharge (eight minutes on the dock will give it one minute in the air).

As Ring founder Jamie Siminoff explained during the preview event, the company has been trying to build a workable camera drone for around a decade, but couldn't overcome certain design challenges until the advancement of AI models that allow the device to handle most of the computing—from route programming to threat detection—via the cloud, so the drones can be smaller and lighter.

According to Ring, when setting up the Ring Drone Cam, you carry it around your house, allowing it to map the interior. It will "intelligently identify rooms and suggest patrol points: spots worth extra attention." When sent out on "patrol," the drone's AI pilot will travel between hotspots, sensing and avoiding furniture and other obstacles along the way.The Ring Drone Cam works with other Ring cameras, so if an alert is triggered somewhere in your home—say, a window opening unexpectedly—the drone will take off to investigate. It has a built-in security light that will make its presence known, so it can also act as a deterrent, though the screaming sound of its spinning propellers will accomplish that just as well.

According to Ring, the drone camera can deliver peace of mind whether you're home or away, and admittedly I do like the idea of being able to check on my pets or make sure no pipes have burst while I'm at work or on vacation (though admittedly you can get the same sort of monitoring without involving an AI device that looks like a mini version of the flying robots from The Terminator).

I admit that the Ring Drone Cam seems pretty cool, provided I don't think about it too much. I don't know that I really feel the need to have every inch of my home covered in security cameras, but I do like the idea that the drone could, for example, go to check out what's going on if one of my smoke alarms' temperature sensors reports that one spot in the house is all of a sudden hotter than it should be.

If you're ready to enter this brave new world of security, you'll have to wait a bit longer: The Ring Drone Camera isn't expected to ship until January 2027, but you can sign up to be alerted when it is available for preorder now.

#3541. WoW: Forever Weekly Player Numbers Are The Highest For Blizzard’s MMO In 15 Years

World of Warcraft: Forever continues to break ground for developer Blizzard, which revealed new stats related to Forever's already record-breaking launch.

Forever launched on November 4, and it didn't take long for Blizzard to announce that the game, the third major version of Blizzard's MMORPG, was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent and returning players.

Now, Blizzard is revealing more launch stats. Holly Longdale, executive producer and vice president for WoW, announced on social media that Forever has "more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years."

The tidbit translates to Forever having more weekly active players than any WoW release since the game's 2010 Cataclysm expansion. That's quite the accomplishment considering that time period also includes massively popular expansions like 2016's Legion and the release of WoW Classic in 2019.

That wasn't the only statistic Blizzard had to share. It revealed that more than 15 million characters have been created in Forever, with nearly 1.5 billion quests completed so far. It also shared the game's deadliest boss, Archmage Arugal from the Shadowfang Keep dungeon, as well as nearly 29 million PvP kills and almost 197 million player deaths. You can check out the full statistics below.

While fun, Blizzard's stats don't reveal the numbers that more than a few players are likely curious about, like Forever's most popular races and classes. For that, players have to rely on third-party fan sites that have tracked Forever statistics since launch.

Forever's launch may be breaking records, but that wasn't enough to score the MMO a nod at The Game Awards 2026. In other WoW Forever news, Blizzard recently made yet another big change to dungeons.

#3539. WoW: Forever Exploit Lands Streamers In Hot Water After Farming Thousands Of Gold

A lucrative World of Warcraft: Forever dungeon-farming exploit that netted some players hundreds of gold per hour has been hotfixed, and Blizzard is taking action against accounts that (temporarily) walked away with thousands in loot.

For the dedicated few who have already reached max level in the new version of Blizzard's MMORPG, a new endgame dungeon, Blackmaw Hold, proved to be quite lucrative. In the dungeon, a room with 30 non-elite enemies proved to be the perfect spot for area-of-effect gold farming, since it's easy to access.

As detailed by Wowhead, the farm was as simple as running to the room in question, killing all the mobs, looting them, resetting the dungeon, and repeating. Not only did the enemies drop anywhere from 25 to 50 silver each, but they also dropped items that could be sold either to a vendor or on the auction house for even more profit.

And some players, including prominent streamers, did just that during Forever's second weekend. One streamer, Ziqo, who was previously in hot water for accepting illegal gold during the game's beta, revealed he made 4,000 gold from the farm. On stream, Ziqo named other streamers who did the same and said his only regret was choosing to sleep for four hours instead of farming longer.

On places like the WoW: Forever subreddit, players worried about the effect such a huge amount of questionably obtained gold would have on the MMO's economy, especially since the game has been out for less than two weeks. Many called on Blizzard to take action against accounts, including streamers, who benefited from the farm.

Blizzard issued a hotfix on November 16, making the enemies from Blackmaw Hold no longer drop loot. In a forum post the following day, Blizzard explained what went wrong and why it was taking action. While Blizzard said finding good farming spots is part of old-school WoW, the enemies players were farming in Blackmaw Hold were incorrectly dropping loot that would normally be reserved for elites, an obvious mistake.

Players who ran the dungeon a few times and "benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong" and don't need to worry, Blizzard said. However, a few "hundred players worldwide" spent "significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies."

Those players are now in more serious trouble. Blizzard locked their ability to engage in Forever's wider economy following the exploit, and said it is removing gold they earned through "exploitative gains." Additionally, "significant abusers" of the exploit will be handed account suspensions.

"As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended," Blizzard said. "We will continue to take action against intentional abuse."

The Blackmaw Hold farm wasn't the first gold controversy in Forever, and it certainly won't be the last. During the game's beta, streamers were caught accepting suspicious amounts of gold and encouraging their communities to illegally buy gold on their behalf. As a result, Blizzard issued suspensions, made in-game changes, and made it clear it would crack down not only on accounts selling illegal gold, but also on those buying or accepting it.

Farming exploits aside, Forever's launch has been relatively smooth, though Blizzard can't seem to decide how much experience players should get in dungeons. Despite Forever's launch breaking WoW concurrent-player records, it still wasn't enough to get the MMO nominated for Best Ongoing Game at The Game Awards 2026.

#3537. Tallulah Willis: I Stayed Out Past My Bedtime to Celebrate My Mom at the Baby2Baby Gala

The whole endeavor began as it usually does, with a search for the perfect dress. Turns out it would be a yellow Carolina Herrera column-shaped confection (if you care), teetering on yellow satin pointed peekaboo-toe platforms, with my first press pass thudding around in my corresponding yellow duchess satin clutch.

Stylist Brad Goreski and his assistant Clarke, who work with my mother, Demi Moore, sourced the ensemble after finding Mom’s beautiful black ruffled two-piece (adorably also Carolina Herrera).

Around 6:50 p.m. on Saturday, my older sisters, Scout (in cocoa-brown beaded Elie Saab) and Rumer (in whimsical archival Vera Wang), florist Eric Buterbaugh, Brad, my mom and I are about to leave her house for the Baby2Baby Gala, an annual fundraiser for the non-profit that dedicated to providing diapers, clothing, and other basic necessities to children and families in need across the country.

Demi is taking photos against a pale brown backdrop when I hear her say, marginally worried, “Yes, the outfit is amazing, but they didn’t give me pockets.” I cannot fault her. A pocket, particularly in an evening gown, creates an entirely different architecture for one’s night.

When we make it to the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, Rihanna is blasting and a gorgeous electric General Motors car, part of the silent auction, is parked out front. I’m holding the bottom of my dress to avoid any “yard sales” on the carpeted floor when I hear, “Is it you? I hope it’s you!” It’s my very new, lovely friend Jackie Tohn, whom I met at a Nobody Wants This premiere party.

Inside, beautifully dressed people laugh and chat. I spot Miranda Kerr, who is both a Baby2Baby board member and major donor, and pass Nara Smith leaning over a dolled-up Elsa Hosk while “Espresso” blasts from overhead speakers.

Table 4 is front and center. Some could say the best seats in the house. Fitting, as Baby2Baby is honoring my mother with the Giving Tree Award tonight. The scene around our table is a frenzy of joyful energy. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

The program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and announces Baby2Baby’s new permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”

Then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for new mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he says.

Then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she says, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

Then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

On the big day, Ann Michael attended the ceremony with Drake when it was revealed he’d be joining the Patriots.

Ann Michael attended one of Drake’s first NFL games. “Just the beginning,” she captioned an Instagram pic of the couple on the sidelines.

Drake exited the game after being sacked in the first quarter. The team hadn’t revealed his official diagnosis or timeline for recovery at the time of Ann Michael’s post.

#3535. GTA 6 Gym Workouts Have A Useful Trick That Saves You A Lot Of Time

You won't get muscles in real life without putting in some work, but fortunately, leveling up your pectorals in Grand Theft Auto 6 is much less strenuous. The only cardio you'll need to do is a series of finger movements on your controller, but admittedly, getting either of the game's protagonists into shape can be time-consuming. Fortunately, there's a trick that can help you cut workout times in half, which I wish I could apply to real life as well.

Essentially, all you need to do in GTA 6 is make sure you're going to the gym as a couple. If you only focus on Jason or Lucia for a workout, then they'll gradually gain muscle and tone up on their own. But if you go as a pair, it doesn't matter who you work out with; both characters will gain and progress on their path toward becoming absolute units.

That makes for a quick way to bulk up, though we still need to talk about Jason's gym etiquette.

This isn't the first time GTA has introduced gym gameplay mechanics to keep your protagonist in shape; back in GTA: San Andreas, players could frequent locations across the map and work on CJ's appearance. Not only could he increase his muscle mass and stamina by pumping iron, but CJ could also learn new fighting styles from trainers along the way. Working out in GTA 6 also has benefits, as lifting weights can improve overall health, while cardio activities like running and biking improve stamina.

You can even track Jason and Lucia's workouts via a smartphone app, and there's an optimal time for them to train to maximize their efforts. You can do that either at a proper gym in the game world or, if you're on a budget, use the set of weights outside Jason's house.

With GTA 6 out in the wild, players are quickly discovering just how much there is to do in Rockstar's massive open-world game. If you're one of them and looking for tips and tricks, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for walkthroughs to help you out.
