#3533. Penélope Cruz Says She and Husband Javier Bardem are “Very Careful” About Choosing When to Work Together

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

"When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it."

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

“I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz said she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a big privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most important thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a big screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”

Cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

“I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he said. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. Landman is making quite the splash down in Texas right now, as people saw the show being filmed at a Texas Christian University game over the weekend. Then, not long after that, Ali Larter posted a photo dump from filming, and it featured one person I never expected to see: Glen Powell.

Of course, I’m well aware that Glen Powell is dating Michelle Randolph, Larter’s on-screen daughter and a veteran of Taylor Sheridan’s shows. He’s also famously from and lives in Texas, which is where Landman is filmed. So, it’s not illogical for him to be around the set of this popular Paramount+ show. However, I was still surprised to see him in the final slide of Larter’s photo dump. Take a look:

In that final slide, you can see Larter posing for a photo with her co-stars, Billy Bob Thornton and Michelle Randolph, as well as Glen Powell.

Now, Landman has actually been filming at Texas Christian University since October, per the university. However, it made headlines over the weekend because Randolph was spotted with the cheerleaders on Saturday during the game against the Kansas State Wildcats.

In Landman, she plays Ainsley Norris, the daughter of Thornton’s Tommy and Larter’s Angela. She’s a student at TCU, and a big part of her storyline has to do with her joining the cheer team. It would seem it will be an even bigger part of her arc in Season 3, seeing as not only was Randolph seen filming at this game, but Larter and Bobbi Salvör Menuez, who play Paigyn, were there too.

To top it all off, Glen Powell was also spotted at the game. As you can see in the third image of this carousel TCU uploaded, the Twisters actor was on the sidelines – which is also where his girlfriend happened to be.

A post shared by TCU (@texaschristianuniversity)

Rumors that Powell and Randolph were dating picked up in late 2025, and the actors went Instagram official in July of this year. Since then, they’ve posted pictures of each other here and there, and the Running Man star’s dog, Brisket, even made a cameo in one of the 1923 actress’s photo dumps.

Speaking of Brisket, Powell’s dog also gives him another tie to Landman. In early 2025, Brisket met up with Demi Moore’s pup, Pilaf. Man, it’s really a small world, and maybe I shouldn’t be shocked that he now has a connection to another star of this Taylor Sheridan show.

Overall, it was very cute to see the Top Gun: Maverick star pop up in a photo dump all about Landman. Clearly, he’s being a supportive partner and cheering Randolph on as she literally cheers on TCU. I also bet it’s pretty cool to just say you get to hang out with her, Ali Larter, Billy Bob Thornton, and Sam Elliott.

Now, I think the question becomes: Could we get Glen Powell on Landman? Taylor Sheridan has a tendency to hire A-listers for his shows, so I don’t think it’s out of the question. Plus, these images make it clear that the Chad Powers star is already literally very close to the production.

#3531. Patrick Mahomes and Wife Brittany Announce Sex of Baby No. 4 With Cake Reveal

Patrick Mahomes and wife Brittany Mahomes have revealed the gender of their fourth child.

“Baby #4🥹🤭,” the Chiefs quarterback, 31, and Brittany, also 31, teased via a joint Instagram video shared on Tuesday, November 17. In the video, the couple were seen in a kitchen with a white cake topped with tiny pink and blue frosted flowers and the words “Oh baby.”

Holding a champagne glass each, the couple, joined by their three children — daughters Sterling, 5, and Golden, 22 months, and son Bronze, 3 — shared a sweet kiss before dunking the tops of their glasses into the cake to see which color frosting would appear once the glassware was retrieved.

To their delight, blue sugary goodness coated the rims of each glass, indicating that they will be welcoming a second son next year.

While Patrick grinned widely over the reveal, Brittany shared her own joy by pounding her fists in the air and jumping up and down. In the meantime, the couple’s family popped confetti cannons that sprayed blue and gold.

The duo then shared another kiss before giving their children hugs, with Brittany raising an arm in the air and Patrick lifting Bronze up high for the cameras.

The clip concluded with further footage of the children making snow angels out of the fallen confetti on the ground before Patrick’s mom, Randi Mahomes, was seen hugging Brittany’s mom, Diana Lindeberg, and the entire clan posed for photos together.

Brittany and Patrick announced on Tuesday, November 10, that they were expanding their brood once again. “Another blessing from God🥹🙏🏼,” they wrote in a joint Instagram post. “& then there were 6🤍.”

Two days later, Patrick said during a Chiefs press conference that he was hoping for a boy. “Obviously, it’s a blessing to have another baby on the way. I’m excited for it,” he said at the time. “I’m hoping that me and Bronze can even up the score.”

He added that besides the baby’s gender, he was mostly “praying for a healthy baby at the end of the day.”

After a reporter pointed out that every time the couple have made a pregnancy announcement in the past, the Chiefs have ended their season with a Super Bowl. The comment put another smile on Patrick’s face.

“I’m hoping. I don’t know if Brittany is,” Patrick responded with a laugh. “But I’m hoping if we can keep that going and get another Super Bowl win with a baby on the way that’d be awesome for sure.”

#3530. GTA 6 Has A Clever PS5 DualSense Trick For Keeping You Under The Speed Limit

While the urge to be an absolute menace in Grand Theft Auto 6 is strong, nothing stops you from playing as a law-abiding citizen who sticks to the speed limit between missions. This option to avoid attracting local law enforcement's attention will probably be best experienced on PS5, thanks to one key advantage: the DualSense controller and its adaptive triggers.

On PS5, GTA 6 players can keep their vehicle from going over the speed limit, as the adaptive triggers provide resistance when you get close to the legal limit. That doesn't mean that you can't break past that barrier, but the adaptive triggers will help you match traffic speed most of the time and stick to legal restrictions. That essentially makes it easier to control your vehicle and gives your index fingers a sense of how hard to press the triggers--useful when you're trying to avoid dinging your car by finding that sweet spot.

This is just one of several vehicle-specific features in GTA 6, as the game borrows a few ideas from modern-day open-world games and puts its own spin on it. For example, you can summon your car via a smartphone app, which involves a Scooter Bros. employee appearing at your location, delivering your ride, and then disappearing into the sunset with the little two-wheeled ride they stashed in your trunk.

Cars appear to be more important than ever in GTA 6, and stealing a fresh set of wheels is also something that has a little more friction to it, as you could boost a junker with an empty tank of fuel or an expensive sports car that has GPS tracking inside of it.

If you're making the trip to Vice City this month, you can check out GameSpot's comprehensive Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub for plenty of tips and tricks.

#3529. GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before

Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, off its throne? The answer is a resounding yes: not only is GTA 6 being reviewed higher than Nintendo's little hero in green, but it's also emerging as one of the highest-rated games of all time.

When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 147 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score.

GTA 6 is only the second game to earn a metascore of 98, and hilariously, it's tied with the original Ocarina of Time from 1998. Historically, GTA games have always had some of the highest review aggregates, especially after the series moved to the third dimension. Starting with GTA 3, mainline entries have all earned metascores in the high 90s, with Grand Theft Auto 4 being the highest-reviewed game in the franchise until GTA 6 came along. Here's a closer look at those metascores over the years.:

  • Grand Theft Auto — No metascore
  • Grand Theft Auto 2 — 70
  • Grand Theft Auto 3 — 97
  • Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — 95
  • Grand Theft Auto 4 — 98
  • Grand Theft Auto 5 — 97

Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it.

"This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's GTA 6 review.

If you're planning to start playing it, you can also check out GameSpot's massive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips and tricks you need to explore Vice City.

#3528. Harry Shum Jr. Honors Late 'Glee' Costar Naya Rivera on 'DWTS'

Harry Shum Jr. looked back on his experience filming Glee during the latest episode of Dancing With the Stars.

“I feel like Dancing With the Stars is synonymous with glee … and to be able to dance to Naya’s version, it means so much to so many people, including myself. We miss you, baby girl,” Shum, 44, said during the semifinals on Tuesday, November 17, after his second dance of the night.

After starting the show with a paso doble to “We Found Love” by Rihanna featuring Calvin Harris, Shum and Jenna Johnson set their quickstep to Mark Ronson’s “Valerie” featuring Amy Winehouse, a song performed by the New Directions during season 2 of Glee. The late Naya Rivera sang lead for the fan-favorite performance.

Ahead of Tuesday’s semifinals, Shum confirmed he and Johnson were using the Glee arrangement for inspiration. “It’ll be sung by the band, the wonderful Dancing With the Stars band. And just that energy, feeling that for a quickstep … it’s gonna be beautiful. Can’t wait for y’all to see it,” he noted in an Instagram Story.

In rehearsals, Shum spoke about how “meaningful” the song was to Glee fans. “Glee definitely changed my life,” he added. “It gave me the opportunity to not only dance, but act. And I never thought I would be able to dance to that song again.”

Both of Shum and Johnson’s dances on Tuesday night earned perfect scores from the judges.

Shum began his career as a backup dancer for pop icons including Jennifer Lopez and Mariah Carey before starring on Glee from 2009 to 2015. The cast weathered a handful of tragedies through the years, including the deaths of Cory Monteith and Mark Salling in 2013 and 2018, respectively. Rivera, meanwhile, died in 2020 after an accidental drowning in California.

“I’m failing miserably to process this news. I always imagined old future senior moments where we would hear your infectious laughter down the hall knowing that our funny bone was in for a treat,” Shum wrote in a tribute to Rivera at the time. “To many people, myself included, you were the life of the party. Not only able to rock when fun was to be had after a long day but that shining friend that was always willing to listen, offer sympathy, perspective and at times, give much needed levity to any situation.”

Shum referred to Rivera as “a beast,” praising her dedication and performance chops.

“You deserved more. … You gave life your all and I hope all the good that you have given to the world will be returned in abundance when you reunite with our brother in the heavenly skies,” he continued. “I’m so grateful for our memories. We will make sure to keep your legacy and spirit alive so Josey will grow up to know the incredible woman you were. Love you, Naya. You are already missed. Eternally.”

Dancing With the Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET.

#3527. Casting Walter White: How ‘Breaking Bad’ Found Bryan Cranston

While the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Thomas] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally said, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”

Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s new play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

We were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”

He’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

We only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I said, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

When I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also said, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”

BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I said, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

It’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

But reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

In the same way that The Sopranos is unthinkable with someone other than James Gandolfini in the role of Tony Soprano, I can’t get my head around the idea of a version of Breaking Bad that doesn’t include Bryan Cranston. But this is Hollywood, and even on basic cable, you don’t just sign up a former sitcom star—­ not even one as gifted as Bryan—­and hand him the starring role in a complex drama without a bit of, shall we say . . . discussion.

MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any big name.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of said, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

The story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

It’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

The truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

So, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

Vince was very passionate. He said he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also said, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”

While some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and said, “We should all just go home. It’s over. That guy’s going to get it.”

VINCE GILLIGAN: We saw a lot of really good actors, several of them now famous names. They never dissuaded me that Bryan was the guy. And luckily, Bryan said yes, because he was up at the same time for a pilot for Fox that was going to pay him . . . well, my understanding is, substantially more money. Like a doctor show. Thank goodness he went with us instead.

#3526. GTA 6’s GTA+ Subscription Includes A Free Supercar, Discounts, And More

Grand Theft Auto 6 is rolling out worldwide, and if you have a GTA+ subscription, you can pick up extra goodies for your trip to Vice City. Developer Rockstar Games has revealed that it'll be evolving its subscription service to cover both GTA Online and GTA 6, and for $8 a month, players can unlock several in-game benefits, including store discounts, more public transit options, and better haggling power.

If you've preordered GTA 6, you'll automatically get a month of GTA+ for free. One thing to note: the services below are only available while you're subscribed, so if your membership expires or you cancel, those perks will no longer be available. Here's a breakdown of what you'll get if you stay subscribed.

Venturas Blvd Elegy supercar and garage

Looks do matter in Vice City, and nothing looks better than a '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy supercar when you hit the streets. This high-speed vehicle can be safely stored in a single-car garage in Crosstown, which also includes a weapon locker and the ability to fence stolen items directly. You'll gain access to it after you complete Chapter 3 in GTA 6.

Transit Service Bonuses

If you'd prefer to rely on public transit, you can grab an upgrade for these facilities. This includes Scooter Bros Premium, premium membership on the RydeMe rideshare app, free scooter, bike, and Seashark rentals, and free rides on Leonida public transportation.

Store discounts

Select businesses across the city will also offer you a 10% discount on their services. Weapons and clothes shops, hairdressers, tattooists, vehicle mod shops, and more are included.

Increased sell value

Selling an eligible vehicle will also net you an extra 10% in cash.

Meanwhile, GTA Online players are also getting plenty of bang for their buck with GTA+ this month, as they can unlock a free car, in-game discounts, the Vinewood Car Club features, bonuses, and more. Are you planning to visit Vice City? Then check out GameSpot's comprehensive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips, tricks, and walkthroughs to give you a leg up as you rise to the top of the crime food chain. From a list of GTA 6 cheat codes to a walkthrough on how to tempt fate by getting a six-star wanted level, there's plenty to dig into here.

Is Season 30 of The Voice making me a little bit country?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spoiler alert! This story discusses the Live Shows' Y2K Week on The Voice Season 30, which aired November 16. Episodes are available to stream the day after they air with a Peacock subscription.

The Voice Live Shows are in full swing on the 2026 TV schedule, and have been narrowing down Season 30’s incredible talent to the Top 10. In the latest episode of NBC’s long-running singing competition, they continued to pay tribute to the hits of the late ‘90s and early 2000s with Part 2 of Y2K Week with Team Riley and Team Kelly. From the Goo Goo Dolls hit “Iris” to The Chicks’ tune “Cowboy Take Me Away” to Keane’s indie rock track “Somewhere Only We Know,” there was a blend of musical genres that traveled all over the map and gave a glimpse into how challenging it will be to continue to cut singers, moving ever closer to the winning coach and star. I need to talk about the country music.

While veteran coach Kelly Clarkson knows firsthand what it takes to win, having taken the title four times in nine seasons, including during her first season as a coach, The Voice newbie Riley Green should not be deterred, as Season 30 is proving to be anyone’s game. Take it from this rock music fan, who’s quickly being won over by one of Team Riley’s country singers. Sure, Kelly has 14-year-old and 16-year-old powerhouse singers on her team – Brianna Cameron, who sang “Reflection” by Christina Aguilera, and Koumba Diallo, who sang the Alicia Key’s hit “Fallin’” – but it’s the teenager on Team Riley that is making the best case for crooning his way to the finals.

Country singer Joe Henley (not to be confused with Joe Hendry) is only 19 and had never played a gig before auditioning for The Voice, which only makes his journey on the show more impressive. After grabbing the attention of Kelly Clarkson and Riley Green during the Blind Auditions, making it through the Battle Rounds, and hands-down reclaiming his spot on Team Riley for Cut Week, he took on Lee Ann Womack’s “I Hope You Dance.”

It's one of those country tracks that has crossed over into the mainstream, with deeply emotional lyrics that I’ve personally connected with and that always pull on my heartstrings when I hear it. It was an unexpected choice to hear the #1 hit covered by a male, but Joe crushed it, reinforcing the possibility that he really could win it all in Season 30.

For a rock girlie to be saying that is a big deal! Just saying!

Sure, Team Adam and Team Kelly have the numbers advantage, with three singers still left on each of their teams while the other coaches only have two. I can’t believe I’m still on the country train, but I actually think that Team has a very good chance of winning in his first season, whether that’s with Joe Henley or the duo Ferryn & Brinkley. He’s proven to have an excellent ear for talent and has given great advice and guidance to his team as their performances have only gotten stronger.

While we already know the competition series will be shaking things up with Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity, we won’t learn who will take it all in Season 30, and if that could be country singer Joe Henley, until December. So, be sure to keep tuning in to NBC on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET until then.

#3524. GTA 6 Passes 17 Million Copies Sold And $1.6 Billion In Revenue On Eve Of Launch

The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 17.07 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.65 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 12.73 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 4.35 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 17.07 million GTA 6 sales so far, 75% are on PS5 and 25% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.23 billion in revenue, compared to $419 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

#3523. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two’s Stock Explodes After High Review Scores, But It’s Still Down Massively This Year

After more than 10 years of waiting, Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally available now (at least in New Zealand and Australia). The anticipation has been sky-high for both consumers and investors alike, and Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, is seeing a huge uplift in its share price today after the game's overwhelmingly positive reviews landed.

The US stock market doesn't officially open until 9:30 AM ET, but ahead of that, Take-Two shares are up close to 7% in pre-market trading. If this holds, it would boost Take-Two's total market cap by billions, and it could go even higher.

Stock analysts expected share value to increase in the lead-up to launch, and many expect it to go higher still due to the expected launches of GTA Online and a PC edition of the game in 2027.

While Take-Two's stock price is popping today, Take-Two remains down close to 20% so far in 2026 and is down about 15% over the past 12 months. Why? No one really knows, because the stock market is fickle. Take-Two's stock price got hammered earlier this year when Google announced new AI software to make games, presumably spooking investors. The stock has not recovered since.

The 52-week high for Take-Two is $265.65, and the 52-week low is $183.86. Take-Two closed on November 17 at $203.93, but is up to $216 in pre-market trading today. As stated, the market opens at 9:30 AM ET today, so check back for more.

GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. "GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," reviewer Tamoor Hussain said.

GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.

#3522. As MAGA Melts Down, MAHA Is Also Breaking Apart—Starting With the Moms

In August 2024, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suspended his presidential campaign and endorsed Donald Trump, bringing his ragtag bunch of supporters—crunchy mamas, anti-vaxxers, and conspiracy theorists; testosterone bros, peptide enthusiasts, and people who put a “COEXIST” bumper sticker on their car in the 1990s—along for the ride. But now that the blue wave or tsunami—pick your tortured water metaphor—has come to pass, the fractures within MAHA threaten to break the movement apart, driven by bitter disappointment with the Trump administration.

“I think we are seeing a fracturing of the MAHA movement as those concerns start pulling people in different directions,” says Sandro Galea, dean of the Bursky School of Public Health at Washington University in St. Louis. Groups that are interested in healthier food are not necessarily the same as groups opposed to vaccines, he points out; it’s not a sure thing that those groups will continue to find common cause.

The crack-up didn’t start with the midterms, though the fact that most MAHA-backed candidates lost certainly accelerated it. Earlier this year, Trump had to withdraw his nomination of MAHA darling Casey Means for surgeon general after her stance on vaccines made it impossible for Republicans to get enough votes to support her confirmation. In May, MAHA ally Marty Makary, the commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration, resigned, reportedly because of pressure from the administration to authorize fruit-flavored vapes. And in October, Calley Means—Casey’s brother—resigned from his high-level post under Secretary Kennedy at Health and Human Services, with MAHA outrage on unmet promises growing.

Three days after the midterms, Joe Rogan released a bomb-throwing, names-naming, two-plus-hour interview with Calley Means, in which the former Kennedy adviser used the word “demonic,” possibly in the literal sense, eight times.

The big takeaway was that Susie Wiles seemed to have told Kennedy to go sit in a corner and play by himself. All roads to Trump went through her office, and according to Means, she slow-walked, watered down, or outright quashed many MAHA priorities. According to Means, she did this primarily because of her and her family’s financial ties to lobbying on behalf of big business.

Wiles did not respond to a request for comment, but a spokesperson for Wiles previously told Axios that these allegations were “outrageous, defamatory, and provably false.”

Means argued that MAHA managed some wins: Trump signed an executive order to boost research on the use of psychedelics for treating mental health conditions. The new food pyramid instructs Americans to eat more steak than oatmeal. (In this economy?) There have been other MAHA victories too: The administration made it easier for Americans to get a handful of unproven injectable peptides, including the “Wolverine stack.” Trump signed an executive order in support of regenerative farming. The administration requested changes to the labels on testosterone products in an effort to make the hormone easier to prescribe—good news for Pete Hegseth’s promise of a “high-T Department of War.” It asked food manufacturers to voluntarily phase out some food dyes. It has sought to reduce the number of recommended childhood vaccines.

Means did not cite the United States recently losing its measles-elimination status as a win, though that was also a result of MAHA talking points.

The MAGA-MAHA mind meld provided plenty for the wellness bros, but precious little of what MAHA moms were expecting from their alliance with Trump. Tiffany Cianci, a high-profile MAHA advocate who goes by @thevinomom on Instagram, says the results were “small things,” not the massive systemic changes that had been promised.

In an emailed statement, a spokesperson for HHS pushed back on this narrative, writing, in part, “HHS has delivered the most sweeping public health reforms in modern history…Across the federal government, the administration has transformed food and nutrition policy, invested more than $1 billion in regenerative agriculture and farm modernization, and taken action to address harmful chemical exposures.”

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. delivers remarks during an event at HHS in August. The event highlighted a series of 'landmark actions' to improve the nation's food.

For the MAHA moms, there are two original sins of Trump 2.0. The first is the administration’s outright support for glyphosate, an herbicide that has been classified as a probable carcinogen by a World Health Organization agency. The second is its failure to put out a definition of ultra-processed foods, which the movement sees as the first step toward curbing those foods, particularly in school lunches. One was never released; Means alleged to Rogan that ultra-processed-food initiatives such as this were stymied by White House officials including Wiles, who he said told him, “I need sugar money.” Reporting found that food CEOs leaned on the White House to make the definition go away.

A White House official said on background that the definition for ultra-processed food remains a priority and is actively being worked on by relevant agencies. White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said that “the MAHA coalition has found a champion in President Trump…The administration has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming.”

However, the Trump administration has arguably hindered research on ultra-processed foods in other ways. A leading scientist who was studying ultra-processed food’s link to diabetes and obesity took early retirement from the National Institutes of Health last year after NIH officials, he said, censored the reporting of some of his study results because the study didn’t prove the hypothesis of ultra-processed-food addiction as they had hoped it would. If he’s to be believed, one of our best hopes for understanding the health risks of ultra-processed foods exited due to the actions of MAHA officials. (Vanity Fair has reached out to HHS for comment on the allegations of censorship; an HHS spokesperson previously told The New York Times, “NIH scientists have, and will, continue to conduct interviews regarding their research through written responses or other means. We remain committed to promoting gold-standard research and advancing public health priorities.”)

“We do have a food supply that’s nearly 70% ultra-processed food,” says Jessica Knurick, a registered dietitian and science communicator on social media. She counters that many of MAHA’s alleged priorities are aligned with the hopes of public health workers and nutritionists—yet the movement writ large has eroded trust in the very professionals who do that work. “They really want fewer environmental toxins. If you want that, you need strong regulation on corporations,” she says. “They voted in an administration that is decisively deregulatory.”

“All of the things that the MAHA movement claimed to have wanted,” she adds, “this administration has legislated in the exact opposite direction.”

See, for instance, the glyphosate debacle. Instead of curbing the herbicide, something for which he’d long been an advocate, Kennedy got on board with Trump’s support of it, including an executive order that actually prioritized production of the chemical under the bizarre guise of national security. Then the administration supported Roundup weed killer manufacturer Monsanto, now owned by Bayer, in a case before the Supreme Court, which resulted in a decision shielding the company from state-level lawsuits brought by those who believed they’d been harmed by the glyphosate-containing product. (Glyphosate-based Roundup products are no longer produced for the US residential market.)

This flew in the face of everything MAHA believed about Kennedy’s priorities. Vani Hari, a MAHA influencer who goes by the Food Babe, has been called both the Jenny McCarthy of food and a Democratic infiltrator. She thinks that the last nearly two years resulted in some positive change. She also tells me that she’s become somewhat disillusioned: “There have also been deeply disappointing decisions, particularly when it comes to glyphosate and pesticides.”

Despite it all, the HHS secretary continues to be deified by the vast majority of MAHA leaders, who don’t blame Kennedy for these setbacks. Cianci, however, blames just about everyone involved. “What I see within MAHA right now is a fracturing into one very, very small sliver that loves the proximity to power and the fundraising. They unfortunately tied their hitch to the wrong horse, which is partisanship,” she says. “And you have the rest of us that actually want our kids to be healthy.”

Supporters of the Make America Healthy Again movement are seen at a news conference on removing synthetic dyes from America's food supply, at the Health and Human Services Headquarters in Washington, DC, 2025.

If there is a road forward for MAHA, it might be best exemplified by Elizabeth Frost, a community health advocate and the leader of MAHA Ohio. She comes by her skepticism of the pharmaceutical industry honestly, after growing up in Appalachian Ohio during the height of the opioid epidemic. She now runs a political consultancy in the state, which she says works with both parties.

Beginning last year, Frost partnered with epidemiologists from Yale to find out how the people of East Palestine, Ohio, were still being affected by toxic exposures after the 2023 derailment of a train filled with hazardous materials. Frost went to bat for the scientists, lending her local grassroots credibility to their study on water quality in the town.

“I think there is a broader anti-corporate movement in America that hasn’t really been given a home with either established party because both parties have their own pet corporate interests,” she tells me. After Kennedy’s ascent, she had hoped for a focus on the MAHA issues that enjoy broad support. “Vaccines are not the most popular issue even for MAHA. Most people in MAHA would prefer for the majority of time to be spent talking about issues that are a little bit more unifying”—rather than something like Steak ’n Shake’s now using beef tallow for its french fries. “It’s just not where people’s hearts are.”

Speaking of no heart: Stephen Miller has been promoted to chief of staff after Wiles was forced out in the wake of the midterms. Both Calley Means and Secretary Kennedy have celebrated the move. “Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration. It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” Kennedy wrote on X.

But some MAHA moms are not so sure about the kraken. Cianci says that within MAHA, “people are very, very, very uncomfortable” with Miller. “If you’re just going to do what you’ve been told to do and take it to the extreme—he’s like the human embodiment of the paper clip problem,” she says.

Frost is similarly concerned about how things might go under Miller. “I don’t expect that on environmental exposures, industrial contamination, a strong streak against corporate influence—I doubt we’re going to get those things,” she says. She is also dismayed by MAHA leadership’s embrace of convicted rapist Russell Brand. “What the hell are we doing?” she wonders.

A person familiar with MAHA thinking who spoke on background counters that while it’s fair to say that Miller might be polarizing, he is also not beholden to corporate interests the way Wiles was, making him far less likely to block the scrutiny of pesticides and healthy food policies.

Cianci, Frost, and Hari all hope that MAHA will survive by focusing on policy over partisanship. “I also believe MAHA’s future must be bipartisan,” Hari wrote in an email.

Cianci sees opposition to data centers as the next big issue on which MAHA can lead. And she hopes that the anti-corporate tilt she sees in MAHA will spread. “We had a record number of candidates get elected to Congress this year that turned down all corporate PAC money. That is indicative of the MAHA movement. That is indicative of anti-corruption. And I think they’re going hand in glove.”

Frost would like to see Republicans work with progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on shared goals, like getting pesticides out of the food supply. She wants legislators to realize that “the way to hold their seat is to work across aisles on issues that their constituents care about.”

Perhaps MAHA can reinvent itself by leveraging some of its most popular issues to make common cause with Democrats. After all, 30% of midterm voters told pollsters that they support the MAHA movement, while many more—the vast majority of Americans—say that food additives and pesticide use should be more regulated. A plurality of Americans do not want data centers in their communities. The movement’s best hope for staying relevant is probably the (currently very pissed) MAHA moms, whose concerns about food and pollution were always the most broadly resonant parts of the MAHA platform—rather than a yen for peptides, beef tallow, or testosterone.

Most people want to be able to afford healthy food and effective health care. Trump’s rule has not made those things more accessible, with high cost of living, massive cuts to Medicaid, the ending of certain Affordable Care Act subsidies, and reductions in federal funding for SNAP benefits.

The challenge with a rebrand is that the connection to MAGA is right there in the name. But Trump’s presidency clearly has a shelf life, and MAHA wants to outlast him. “If anyone has any ideas on how to change the name of a political movement,” Frost says, “let me know.”

What does the future hold for DC Studios?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

To say that DC Studios is in the midst of a big change would be a major understatement. It was announced a little over a week ago that in the aftermath of the Warner Bros./Paramount merger, James Gunn and Peter Safran would step down as co-CEOs of the studio. As a result, film producer (and Marvel Studios alum) Jeremy Latcham will lead the brand moving forward. There may, however, now be reason to believe that DC may be leaving WB and by extension, parent company Skydance. This is all due to some recent rumors.

A common claim that’s been reported in the aftermath of the Gunn/Safran news is that Skydance has acquired a lot of Warner Bros.-amassed debt following the merger. It’s been said that a number of DC Studios’ projects were particularly pricey for the company. In a wide-ranging piece, Page Six mentioned sources who alleged that Supergirl, which flopped at the box office earlier this year, lost WB $135 million. With that, X user @entylawyer alleges that Skydance wants to unload the superhero brand for monetary purposes:

The comic studio heads were fired. They didn't quit. Their boss wants to sell off the entire comic book universe to help get rid of some of that $100B debt.

Of course, all of this should be taken with a massive grain of salt, as Skydance’s David Ellison has not indicated that the company plans to sell DC Studios. If that were to actually happen, though, it would result in the availability of a major asset. If Ellison and co. were to sell it, it could theoretically draw some significant interest on the open market.

I’m honestly just not sure who would seek to acquire DC Studios if Skydance were to theoretically choose to sell it. There’s also the matter of which entertainment company would actually have the money to do it. One of the first brands that comes to mind is obviously The Walt Disney Company, which acquired Marvel Entertainment back in 2009 for $4 billion. However, another brand that should be considered as a hypothetical buyer is Netflix,the company that was set to acquire WB before Paramount made a higher bid.

All of that is just speculation but, of course, James Gunn’s DC exit is real, with him and Peter Safran officially stepping down on December 1. News of Gunn’s departure has generated disappointment from those who were all in on his DC plans, and some have expressed concerns about the future of his DCU continuity. As for the actual decision to part ways with Safran and Gunn, a source for Page Six alleged that their bosses had been in talks with Latcham for weeks ahead of the announcement despite publicly saying otherwise:

It was a little bit strange to have it be so publicly stated that [Gunn and Safran] were safe, and during that time, the [Latcham] process had already been kicked off. They were saying one thing, and then they were actively doing another thing.

Naturally, there are a lot of unknown variables here, and it’s currently unclear as to it or when Skydance might confirm or deny the rumor that DC Studios will be sold. In the meantime, there are still film projects from the brand that are in different stages of development as James Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow is set to hit theaters on July 9 amid the 2027 movie schedule. Matt Reeves’ The Batman: Part II is also filming right now and will hit theaters on February 18, 2028.

PS5 Pro consoles have been hard to find lately, but there is a trick to getting one: All you need is superb basketball skills and membership on an NBA team based in the state that inspired Grand Theft Auto 6's location. #3519. 10 Shows Like 'Minimum Wage' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Spinning off of a popular web series, Netflix's Minimum Wage is currently in the middle of a 28-episode first-season run. If that sounds like a lot of episodes for a show in 2026, keep in mind that they're generally less than 15 minutes each, which is perfect for your overloaded to-watch list—especially when they go down so easily. This cringe workplace mockumentary follows the crew of teenagers running a failing pizza place and making (you guessed it) minimum wage; they're under enormous pressure from their boss (Randall Park) to save the business and their one dumb source of income.

The punchy episodes will leave you plenty of time to explore other streaming shows dealing with the utter ridiculousness of the modern workplace. Here are 10 to get you started.

Workplace comedies usually revolve around white-collar office environments (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, 30 Rock, Parks and Recreation, etc.). Like Minimum Wage, Superstore instead follows the staff of Cloud 9, a generic big-box retailer. The show’s deep bench and diverse cast are largely focused on the jokes, but much of that comedy involves the relatable situation of working a job that demands commitment and a smiley attitude in the face of both entitled customers and obnoxious bosses. It's a different venue and age bracket, but a nutty workplace is a nutty workplace. Stream Superstore on Hulu and Peacock.

We're moving away from the workplace and aging things up a bit, but no worries: the name is a little ironic given that the codependent, co-habitating twenty-somethings of the title are hardly mature. Five friends are cohabiting in the childhood home of Samir (Malik Elassal), and dealing with the uniquely Gen-Z humiliations around dating, work, and even health insurance. Only one member of the group has an actual reasonably good job, while career paths for the others include being a temp, waiter, and a part-time ballet instructor. Stream Adults on Hulu.

This offbeat workplace comedy kicks off with a fabulous premise: Jeong Bok-dong (Kim Byung-chul) was a high-level director in a major corporation until one bad meeting saw him demoted. To president! ...of the company's failing Pegasus Mart offshoot. Bok-dong makes it his mission to get revenge by bankrupting the store, hiring eccentrics to execute eccentric, entirely whackadoo plans and accidentally getting Pegasus noticed by customers, who quickly make it more popular than ever. Think The Producers, but in retail. Stream Pegasus Market on Tubi.

It might sound a little (or a lot) niche, but we’ve seen enough headlines about the working conditions at many video game production houses to understand why a workplace comedy set against such a backdrop would make for a dark and juicy comedy. Charlotte Nicdao and Rob McElhenney are the leads, playing a brilliant workaholic and an unsociable egomaniac, respectively, and the chemistry between them gives the show more than enough spark. There's also a four-episode spin-off called Side Quest. Stream Mythic Quest.

A half-hour comedy-drama with an emphasis on the comedy, Gentefied follows three Mexican-American cousins who have built lives in Los Angeles, only to be faced with a new challenge: the looming gentrification of the neighborhood they helped to build via their family's taco shop. Gentefied has a baked-in sense of place and culture and a lot of heart; the second season is even better than the first. Stream Gentefied on Netflix.

Perhaps there's a bit of counter-programming in this dramedy about a couple of scrappy New York City outsiders, but there's a fundamental goofiness to this show about a couple of nice guys who are great at getting themselves into trouble, and equally good at talking themselves out of it. Bryan Greenberg plays Ben Epstein, a quiet guy with any number of big ideas, while Victor Rasuk plays the outgoing, often shameless Cam Calderon; together they manage a startup clothing business with the benefits of neither money nor experience, amiably hustling their way to success, maybe. Stream How to Make It in America on HBO Max and Netflix.

Debuting at the beginning of the Obama administration before getting a surprise revival just a couple of years ago, Party Down is an acclaimed cult sitcom for the ages—lots of laughs, low ratings, and always worth rediscovering. A group of six (or so) struggling LA actors and writers work as cater waiters for a fancy company, with every episode into a new and wildly absurd situation, even as their aspirations far outstrip their actual lives. Stream Party Down on Prime Video and Netflix.

A legitimate sitcom that just happens to be set in Northern Ireland during the violent Troubles of the 1990s, when clashes between nationalists and unionists frequently resulted in violence. It’s a fascinating contrast, brought to life by a writer and creator (Lisa McGee) who lived it. It’s also laugh-out-loud funny—though it doesn’t make any allowances for audiences unaccustomed to Irish accents, so don’t feel bad if you need subtitles until you get the hang of it. Erin, Orla, Clare, and Michelle are joined by James, the only male student at their Catholic girls' school, dealing with normal growing-up stuff in absurd times. This world is a far cry from that of Minimum Wage, but Lisa McGee's sense of the absurd connects both shows—if the setting is a bit more dramatic, the comedy is just as wonderfully silly. Stream Derry Girls on Netflix.

Not a comedy! But about as good an indication of where we are in the modern global workplace as you're likely to find. Hyuk‑jun is a young guy saddled with debt who signs on for some part-time work at a job agency...at 50x the going rate, no less (should've been a red flag). Each new assignment places him in new and increasingly horrific situations, with increasingly arbitrary-seeming rules. But, hey, in 2026, it's a living. Stream Dead-End Job on Netflix.

It's an office (obviously) and not a pizza joint, but the point here is kinda that white-collar jobs in the 21st century can be at least as soul-killing as working customer service. The Office inherited some of the finer tropes of the workplace comedy (mostly involving tossing together a group of weirdos overly invested in their jobs) while also launching a million mockumentary-style shows, running for nine seasons, and becoming one of the most popular shows of its era. Stream The Office on Peacock.

#3518. Billy Crystal Answers the Proust Questionnaire

Which historical figure do you most identify with?

My wife, Janice. Fearless, smart, optimistic, hilarious, loving…adored by all.

What is the trait you most deplore in yourself?

Self-doubt. Wait, now I’m not sure of the answer. Was that okay? Can we come back to that one?

What is the trait you most deplore in others?

From my dressing room to backstage—standing alone in the dark, a deep breath, and then feeling it’s time and walking out into the light.

What do you consider the most overrated virtue?

What do you dislike most about your appearance?

I’d rather not say, and thank you for your attention to this matter!

Which words or phrases do you most overuse?

“Sorry, I didn’t see your text till now.”

That my father died when I was 15 and never got to see my family, my career, and the man I think I am.

What or who is the greatest love of your life?

In the hospital waiting room, when my girls were born, and the doctor said everyone was fine.

Which talent would you most like to have?

If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be?

I’d stop worrying about everyone all the time.

If you could change one thing about your family, what would it be?

That they’d finally understand why I worry about everyone all the time

What do you consider your greatest achievement?

We raised two fantastic daughters who became good, hard-working, honest people and great spouses and mothers in the middle of this business.

If you were to die and come back as a person or thing, what do you think it would be?

If you could choose what to come back as, what would it be?

I lost them all, so I’d have to say my memory.

What do you regard as the lowest depth of misery?

Love, empathy, loyalty, a sense of humor, and a handful of quarters for the parking meters.

Hemingway, David Sedaris, Neil Simon, Herb Gardner, Arthur Miller, Victor Hugo.

Santiago, the fisherman in The Old Man and the Sea.

Picasso, Muhammad Ali, Mickey Mantle, Buster Keaton, Sid Caesar, Mel Brooks, JFK, Alan Shepard—and Jim Redmond, a father who ran out of the stands at the ’92 Olympics to help his son, Derek, who had torn a hamstring in his race and was struggling to stand up and continue. They held onto each other and crossed the finish line together. Perfect.

Holding Janice’s hand. Ready, not frightened, satisfied, and with a smile and a goodbye to my family. And if there’s a laugh, that’s the last thing I hear? That would be great.

#3517. Musician Ryan Adams, 52, Is Engaged to Kate Farr, 22, After 6 Months of Dating

Country music star Ryan Adams is reportedly engaged to fellow musician Kate Farr.

“I’ve never been happier in my life. Kate is the most fascinating, kindest nerd I’ve ever met. She’s my best friend, and I’ve never been happier. Here’s to love,” Adams told TMZ on Tuesday, November 17. The outlet noted that Adams, 52, and Farr, 22, got engaged after six months of dating.

Us has reached out to a representative for Adams for comment.

The outlet also reported that Adams, who is the ex-husband of Mandy Moore, and Farr, a writer and producer who now works in the music industry, met through mutual friends earlier this year. “While the two started out as friends, things quickly turned romantic,” the outlet stated.

A photo of two hands was also published by the outlet, seemingly of Farr’s atop Adams,’ with the top donning a diamond set against gold on its ring finger.

Less than one month again, Adams shared his adoration for Farr in the comments section of an Instagram post she shared. The October 21 carousel, which included three close-up snaps of Farr demurely gazing off camera, attracted Adams’ comment, “Just stopping by to tell you I love you so very much and I hear you rattling around upstairs. ❤️.”

Farr wrote in response, “WEIRDO!!! jk I love you 💛,” which drew a string of red heart emojis from Adams.

TMZ also reported that Farr “moved to Los Angeles to be with Ryan … and the two are now living together,” with plans to leave California one day to move “back to the Midwest … to be closer to family.”

Adams was married to Moore, 42, from March 2009. In January 2015, the former couple separated and their divorce was finalized in June the following year. In the aftermath of her marriage breakdown, Moore alleged in an interview with The New York Times that she was the victim of psychological abuse at the hands of Adams.

The article, which included seven women’s allegations of emotional abuse and sexual misconduct against Adams, including Moore, stated that she was at a pivotal point in her own musical career.

“Music was a point of control for him,” she was quoted as saying in the February 2019 article. “He would always tell me, ‘You’re not a real musician, because you don’t play an instrument.’”

Moore, who is now married to fellow musician Taylor Goldsmith and shares three children with him, also noted that she would once write songs with Adams, which he promised to record but never did.

“His controlling behavior essentially did block my ability to make new connections in the industry during a very pivotal and potentially lucrative time — my entire mid-to-late 20s,” Moore said at the time.

The outlet noted at the time that Adams, through his lawyer, referred to Moore’s depiction of their relationship to be “completely inconsistent with his view of the relationship,” adding that he supported her “well-deserved professional success.”

He issued a further statement to Us in the hours following the Times article going live.

“I am not a perfect man and I have made many mistakes. To anyone I have ever hurt, however unintentionally, I apologize deeply and unreservedly,” the statement to Us read at the time. “But the picture that this article paints is upsettingly inaccurate. Some of its details are misrepresented; some are exaggerated; some are outright false. I would never have inappropriate interactions with someone I thought was underage. Period. As someone who has always tried to spread joy through my music and my life, hearing that some people believe I caused them pain saddens me greatly. I am resolved to work to be the best man I can be. And I wish everyone compassion, understanding and healing.”

#3516. The GTA 6 Map Is Truly, Truly Massive (Of Course)

Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived--at least in New Zealand and Australia. Lots of people are playing the game already and have made a number of discoveries, including just how massive the map is.

Even though we knew the GTA 6 map would be big--it has more playable space than GT4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined--seeing the map for yourself shows off its truly gargantuan scale.

The streamer N3on showed off the entire GTA 6 map, and it's ... large. As confirmed previously, GTA 6 takes place in the state of Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida. The central hub is Vice City itself (GTA's version of Miami), but the game takes players well beyond that to numerous surrounding counties.

GTA 6 also carries the franchise's "fog of war" tradition forward, so that's why you don't see specific details on the map in N3on's video. As players find new places, they will show up more clearly on the map.

But what's obvious at this point is that the GTA 6 map is gigantic. We can only wonder how long it may take to drive from one side to the other, or get all the way down to GTA 6's version of the Southernmost point in the continental US, Key West. GTA 6's version of the Florida Keys is called Leonida Keys.

GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. “GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7,” reviewer Tamoor Hussain said.

GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.

After GTA 6 reviews came online, shares of Rockstar owner Take-Two ripped higher, but the company is still down massively this year and over the past 12 months.

For more on GTA 6, including preload information, preorder bonuses, and release times, check out our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3515. How Patrick Stewart Felt After His Fight With James Corden At The Glamour Awards

Join The Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Here's how the icon felt after his fight with the celebrity host.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Amidst all the tributes and wonderful stories about Patrick Stewart that hit the internet after his passing, one other viral video stood out. Stewart's fight with actor and comedian James Corden onstage at the 2011 Glamour Awards was a rare public outburst by the legendary Star Trek actor, and one that he deeply regretted as the years passed.

For those unfamiliar, the video went viral back then when Stewart took the stage and criticized Corden, the host, for looking disinterested between awards. Corden told Stewart to "get on with presenting," which then escalated to Stewart telling the audience he could see Corden's belly sticking out from the back row. Corden jabbed back that he could see Stewart "dying" onstage due to his age, and after one odd joke involving the Jonas Brothers, the moment ended. People have seen that, but fewer might know how Stewart felt afterward.

Stewart later expressed deep regret about the incident while speaking about it to Classic FM (via Glamour). The Star Trek actor admitted he'd been drinking, and it all went off the rails once he took the stage:

My part of the evening came late and it was alcohol (that prompted the remark), I'm afraid. I went too far, I was somewhat out of control. I have nothing but admiration for Mr Corden. I still blush in remembrance of it.

Buzzfeed also reported that Stewart said elsewhere he was upset by a comment Corden made toward another actress earlier in the evening. He began to drink and, unfortunately, made comments that he regretted. Fortunately, he also confirmed that he'd spoken to the Corden since then, and they agreed to bury the hatchet.

The resurfaced viral video was the most I've seen of James Corden since he retired from late-night, and based on how he spoke about the event, I'm sure he wasn't thrilled to see it back in the news either. The comedian later said he had zero problem with Sir Patrick Stewart, and said that despite how it looked at the moment, he was not mad:

I couldn't have less of a problem with him. He just went for it, he was unscripted, and I've no idea where it was going... And I wish I hadn't looked like I was so angry. Because I was just bemused. I'm not entirely sure what he wanted to happen, but I'm sure what happened wasn't what he wanted. But you know, he's Sir Patrick Stewart and he's great. Everyone's allowed a mistake. My hunch is he's a nice guy.

It's important to know the context of how both sides felt after the fact, because unfortunately, I think people unfairly pushed a narrative about the interaction that wasn't true. The implication was that Patrick Stewart hated James Corden, who has been a polarizing figure since stepping into the limelight.

In reality, the moment went down as one of Stewart's biggest embarrassments, and went against many of the other pleasant interactions that the world knew him for. I'm glad that he found the time to reconcile with Corden after what happened all those years ago, but it's sad to see it resurface again after his death.

CinemaBlend continues to pay respects to Patrick Stewart and offers condolences to his friends and family as they mourn his death. I'm sure more stories about the actor will surface ahead of his appearance in Avengers: Doomsday, which is out in theaters on December 18th.
